'''Shinedown''' is an American [[Rock music|rock]] band from [[Jacksonville, Florida]], formed by singer [[Brent Smith]] in 2001 after the dissolution of his previous band, Dreve. Smith, still under contract with [[record label]] [[Atlantic Records]], recruited the band's original lineup of Jasin Todd as guitarist, [[Brad Stewart]] on bass, and Barry Kerch on drums. Consistent for the first two album cycles, several lineup changes followed in the late 2000s, eventually stabilizing with Smith and Kerch alongside [[Zach Myers]] on guitar and [[Eric Bass]] on bass. The group has released seven studio albums: ''[[Leave a Whisper]]'' (2003), ''[[Us and Them (Shinedown album)|Us and Them]]'' (2005), ''[[The Sound of Madness]]'' (2008), ''[[Amaryllis (Shinedown album)|Amaryllis]]'' (2012), ''[[Threat to Survival]]'' (2015), ''[[Attention Attention]]'' (2018), and ''[[Planet Zero]]'' (2022).

Shinedown has the most number one singles on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Mainstream Rock (chart)|Mainstream Rock]] charts with 21,<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/shinedown-mainstream-rock-airplay-record-killing-fields-1236065824/|title=Shinedown Has 21st Mainstream Rock Airplay No. 1 with 'Killing Fields'|last=Rutherford|first=Kevin|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=September 12, 2025|access-date=September 13, 2025}}</ref> and all of their released singles have reached the top five on the chart. Additionally, on June 3, 2021, Shinedown was ranked number one by ''Billboard'' on the Greatest of All Time Mainstreams Rock Artists chart released to celebrate the Mainstream Rock chart's 40th anniversary.<ref>{{cite magazine |first=Kevin |last=Rutherford|title=Shinedown & Days of the New Rule Greatest of All Time Mainstream Rock Charts |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9581948/shinedown-days-of-the-new-top-greatest-of-all-time-mainstream-rock-charts/|date=June 3, 2021|access-date=July 9, 2021}}</ref> To date, the band has sold more than 10 million records worldwide.<ref name="LATimesSmith"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sidestagemagazine.com/shinedown-breaks-record-for-most-1s-on-billboard-mainstream-rock-songs-chart-with-atlas-falls/|title=Shinedown Breaks Record For Most #1s On Billboard Mainstream Rock Songs Chart with "Atlas Falls"|date=August 18, 2020|access-date=October 5, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128103832/http://www.sidestagemagazine.com/shinedown-breaks-record-for-most-1s-on-billboard-mainstream-rock-songs-chart-with-atlas-falls/|archive-date=January 28, 2022}}</ref>

==History==
===2000–2004: Formation and ''Leave a Whisper''===
The band's origins trace back to [[frontman]] [[Brent Smith]]'s prior band, Dreve, which had signed a record deal with [[Atlantic Records]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FyF4MiYzhtwC&q=dreve+atlantic&pg=PA118|title=Rock Scars|first=James|last=Hester|date=November 23, 2016|publisher=iUniverse|isbn=9781440127731|via=Google Books}}</ref><ref name="ARRetro">{{cite web|url=http://www.atlanticrecords.com/posts/songwriting-and-second-chances-brent-smith-shinedown-20376|title=Songwriting and Second Chances with Brent Smith of Shinedown - Atlantic Records Official Blog|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203101016/http://www.atlanticrecords.com/posts/songwriting-and-second-chances-brent-smith-shinedown-20376|archive-date=February 3, 2022}}</ref> The [[record label]], unhappy with Dreve as a whole, dropped the band prior to releasing an album, but retained Smith, who they felt was worth developing separately as an artist.<ref name="SubAttention">{{cite news | last=Shotwell| first=James| title =Your Attention Please: Brent Smith on Shinedown's bold new album| publisher =Substream| date =April 11, 2018| url =https://substreammagazine.com/2018/04/brent-smith-shinedown-interview-2018/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> Atlantic signed Smith to a development deal where record representatives helped him with his song writing ability, and helped him recruit members for a new band, which would become Shinedown.<ref name="SubAttention"/><ref name="ARRetro"/><ref name="rock.about">{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Grierson|url=http://rock.about.com/od/shinedown/p/shinedown.htm|title=Hard Rock With Grunge Roots Powers Shinedown|date=November 19, 2017|access-date=January 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803125404/https://www.liveabout.com/shinedown-biography-and-profile-2898311|archive-date=August 3, 2020}}</ref> Smith moved to [[Jacksonville, Florida]] and began work on the project in 2001.<ref name="originalineup"/> The first member he recruited was bassist [[Brad Stewart]], through local Jacksonville [[music producer]] Pete Thornton.<ref name="originalineup">{{cite web|first=Keith|last=McDonald|url=http://www.metal-rules.com/interviews/shinedown-May2004.htm|title=Interview with Shinedown |publisher=Metal-Rules.com |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> Smith and Stewart began recording demos together in a small local studio, whose owner recommended they meet with her fiancé, guitarist Jasin Todd, who Smith brought in as the third member.<ref name="originalineup"/> The original lineup was rounded out by drummer Barry Kerch, who was the seventh drummer the band had auditioned for the spot.<ref name="originalineup"/> The four worked together on creating demos, and submitted their work-in-progress material to Atlantic, who approved of the material and green-lighted a full-length album.<ref name="originalineup"/>

The resulting work was the band's debut album, ''[[Leave a Whisper]]'', which was released May 27, 2003.<ref name="Leave a Whisper">{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Loftus|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/leave-a-whisper-mw0000030529|title=Leave a Whisper - Shinedown - Songs, Reviews, Credits - AllMusic|website=AllMusic|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> While not an immediate success, through the extensive touring and successful singles, eventually certified platinum by the [[RIAA]] in the United States, indicating sales of over 1 million.<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Wildsmith|url=http://www.thedailytimes.com/entertainment/shinedown-front-man-finds-a-new-way-of-life-during/article_81697d82-05ee-5af9-9444-d65db07108c3.html|title=Shinedown front man finds a new way of life during making of 'Amaryllis'|website=The Daily Times|date=February 6, 2013|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> Four singles were released from the album: "[[Fly from the Inside]]", "[[45 (Shinedown song)|45]]", a cover of the [[Lynyrd Skynyrd]] song "[[Simple Man (Lynyrd Skynyrd song)|Simple Man]]", and "[[Burning Bright (song)|Burning Bright]]".<ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Davis|url=http://www.knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=3009|title=Exclusive! Interview With Shinedown Vocalist Brent Smith|website=KNAC.com|date=May 17, 2004|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref><ref name="Leave a Whisper"/> All four singles charted in the top five of the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Mainstream Rock (chart)|Mainstream Rock]] charts, peaking at fifth, third, fifth, and second, respectively.<ref name="Chartpg1">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/shinedown/chart-history/rtt/|title=Shinedown - Chart history - Mainstream Rock|website=Billboard.com|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref> The band toured extensively in support of the album, playing over 400 live shows over the course of 2003 and 2004.<ref name="AMUAT">{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Loftus|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/us-and-them-mw0000170855|title=Us and Them - Shinedown - Songs, Reviews, Credits - AllMusic|website=[[AllMusic]] }}</ref> The band ended up touring for 24 months straight, doing various tours with [[Van Halen]], [[Seether]], and [[Three Doors Down]].<ref name="MTVHardRock">{{cite web|first=Alyssa|last=Rashbaum|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1495763/shinedown-have-taken-a-shine-to-being-on-the-road/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170315085250/http://www.mtv.com/news/1495763/shinedown-have-taken-a-shine-to-being-on-the-road/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 15, 2017|title=Shinedown Have Taken A Shine To Being On The Road|website=MTV.com|date=January 11, 2005|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> The band later released a live DVD titled ''[[Live from the Inside]]'' that documented the live shows of the touring cycle.<ref name="AllMusicBioProse">{{cite web|first=Eduardo|last=Rivadavia|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/shinedown-mn0000028002/biography|title=Shinedown - Biography & History|website=[[AllMusic]]|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>

===2005–2006: ''Us and Them''===
The band did not start work on a follow-up album until 2005, with the band finding the touring lifestyle too hectic to start writing or recording material.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/interviews/shinedowns_jasin_todd_we_wrote_the_best_album_we_could.html|title=Shinedown's Jasin Todd: 'We Wrote The Best Album We Could'|website=Ultimate-Guitar.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> This, however, left the band with limited time to record new music, with their record label pressuring the band to get the album out in a six-month time period.<ref name="PGA1"/> Despite the time restrictions, the label did not pressure the band on the album's musical direction after the commercial success of ''Leave a Whisper''.<ref name="GuitarPlayer1"/> The band worked with [[music producer]] Tony Battaglia, and chose to go in a more "mature" and "stripped down" direction for the album's sound, Kerch describing it as just "pure rock."<ref name="PGA1">{{cite web|url=http://puregrainaudio.com/interviews/interview-with-shinedown-bassist-brad-stewart-drummer-barry-kerch|title=Interview with Shinedown bassist Brad Stewart & drummer Barry Kerch|first=Christopher|last=Gonda|website=PureGrainAudio.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref><ref name="GuitarPlayer1"/> During the same time, the band was also approached by [[Hollywood Records]] to record a song for a [[tribute album]] for the band [[Queen (band)|Queen]], something the band agreed to out of their respect for the band.<ref name="PGA1"/> They recorded a cover of the track "[[Tie Your Mother Down]]," which was released on ''[[Killer Queen: A Tribute to Queen]]'' (2005).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/queen-killer-queen-tribute-album-track-listing-revealed/|title=Queen: 'Killer Queen' Tribute Album Track Listing Revealed|date=July 1, 2005|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>

The band released their second studio album, ''[[Us and Them (Shinedown album)|Us and Them]]'', on October 4, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/us-and-them-mw0000170855|title=Us and Them - Shinedown - Songs, Reviews, Credits - AllMusic|website=AllMusic|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> The album debuted higher than ''Leave a Whisper'' on the ''Billboard'' 200 chart, peaking at number 23 versus ''Leave a Whisper'''s number 53 peak, but the album ultimately sold less than its predecessor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-zach-myers-carnival-of-madness-music-industry/|title=Shinedown's Zach Myers Talks Carnival of Madness, Music Industry + More|website=Loudwire|date=September 9, 2013 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>  Despite this, the band's three singles from the album, "[[Save Me (Shinedown song)|Save Me]]", "[[I Dare You (Shinedown song)|I Dare You]]", and "[[Heroes (Shinedown song)|Heroes]]" ended up being more successful than their prior album's singles.<ref name="billboardUAT"/><ref>[http://www.411mania.com/music/columns/11980/411Mania-Exclusive-Interview:-Brent-Smith-Of-Shinedown.htm 411Mania Interview] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120920212416/http://www.411mania.com/music/columns/11980/411Mania-Exclusive-Interview:-Brent-Smith-Of-Shinedown.htm |date=2012-09-20 }}</ref> The lead single, "Save Me" was the band's first to reach the number one spot on the Mainstream Rock Charts, and held the position for twelve weeks in a row.<ref name="Chartpg1"/><ref name="billboardUAT">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/shinedown-cage-the-elephant-no-1s-rock-charts/|title=Shinedown & Cage the Elephant Add New No. 1s on Rock Charts|website=Billboard.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> The second single, "I Dare You", also peaked at number 2 on the same chart.<ref name="Chartpg1" /> Notably, both songs were also the band's first to have crossover success on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot 100]] charts, hitting 72 and 88 respectively.<ref name="Hot100">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/279123/shinedown/chart|title=Shinedown|website=Billboard.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>

The band again toured heavily in support of the album, including the 2006 iteration of the [[SnoCore Tour]] with [[Seether]], [[Flyleaf (band)|Flyleaf]], and [[Halestorm]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/60048/seether-reteams-with-shinedown-on-snocore-trek|title=Seether Reteams With Shinedown On Snocore Trek|website=Billboard.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>  and later opening for [[Godsmack]] and [[Rob Zombie]]  co-headlining tour of North America.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-confirmed-as-opening-band-on-godsmack-rob-zombie-tour/|title=Shinedown Confirmed As Opening Band On Godsmack/Rob Zombie Tour|date=June 11, 2006|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Promotional support came from other areas as well; then-''[[American Idol]]'' contestant [[Chris Daughtry]] performed "I Dare You" live on the show, helping its crossover appeal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.today.com/popculture/taylor-hicks-gets-funky-idol-wbna12601578|title=Taylor Hicks gets 'funky' on 'Idol'|first=Craig|last=Berman|website=Today.com|date=May 3, 2006 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> and was used as a theme song for [[WrestleMania 22]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://whatculture.com/wwe/11-greatest-wwe-wrestlemania-songs-ever?page=2|title=11 Greatest WWE WrestleMania Songs Ever|date=March 17, 2016|website=WhatCulture.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> The success of the singles helped propel sales of the album in the long run, ultimately being certified platinum by the RIAA on March 19, 2018, signifying 1 million album sales.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=SHINEDOWN&ti=US+AND+THEM|title=Shinedown|website=riaa.com|access-date=October 5, 2020}}</ref>

===2007–2010: ''The Sound of Madness''===
Work on a third studio album began in early 2007. While the record label requested an album to be created in six months, Smith declined, stating that he was not happy with the results of working under the time restraints on the last album, and wished to take his time on the album.<ref name="AlwaysInterview">{{cite web|url=https://alwaysacoustic.com/shinedown-brent-smith-2008-interview/|title=Shinedown Interview with Brent Smith|first=Always|last=Acoustic|date=September 20, 2012|website=AlwaysAcoustic.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> The label agreed to this, ultimately allowing Smith to take 18 months to prep the album.<ref name="AlwaysInterview"/> Part of the long development time was due to internal issues within band members; during this time, Smith fired both Stewart and Todd from the band.<ref name="PilotOnline">{{cite web|url=http://pilotonline.com/entertainment/music/shinedown-has-wrung-hits-out-of-hard-times-and-survived/article_7c12d742-e23f-50bb-81e0-53533850d8de.html|title=Shinedown has wrung hits out of hard times and survived to enjoy good times|first=Alan Sculley|last=Correspondent|website=PilotOnline.com|access-date=October 17, 2017|archive-date=March 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170309031536/http://pilotonline.com/entertainment/music/shinedown-has-wrung-hits-out-of-hard-times-and-survived/article_7c12d742-e23f-50bb-81e0-53533850d8de.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Smith let Stewart go due to disagreements with the direction of the band, feeling that Stewart was no longer happy or committed to the band.<ref name="AlwaysInterview"/> Todd was fired due to major disagreements with Smith, and personal problems that were getting in the way of the band.<ref name="AlwaysInterview"/><ref name="SPInterview">{{cite web |url=http://www.starpulse.com/a-conversation-with-brent-smith-of-shinedown-1847890668.html |title=A Conversation with Brent Smith of Shinedown |access-date=2017-03-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170317055159/http://www.starpulse.com/a-conversation-with-brent-smith-of-shinedown-1847890668.html |archive-date=March 17, 2017 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Then-touring guitarist, Zach Myers, later recounted that both Smith and Todd were going through significant [[substance abuse]] issues at the time with drugs and alcohol, which lead to much infighting between the two.<ref name="PilotOnline"/> The band almost broke up during the period, but Smith firing Todd and stopping his drug use helped eliminate the internal issues, and helped the band move forward.<ref name="PilotOnline"/><ref name="SPInterview"/>

Smith spent much of 2007 writing new material with [[Rick Beato]] of Black Dog Sound Recording Studios in Stone Mountain, GA, for the third album.<ref name="SPInterview"/> Sessions were prolific, with Smith writing over 60 songs during the period, though that he now lacked a guitarist and bassist was a constant concern.<ref name="AlwaysInterview"/> Smith recruited a number of studio musicians for its recording sessions; Dave Barrett contributed most of the album's guitars, [[Tim Pierce]] contributed some additional guitar, and [[Chris Chaney]] contributed most of the album's bass guitar.<ref name="SPInterview"/> The rough demos were sent from the record label to music producer [[Rob Cavallo]], who, upon hearing them, told Smith he wanted to produce the album.<ref name="SPInterview"/>

[[File:Shinedown concert.jpg|thumb|Shinedown live in 2008]]

The final result, ''[[The Sound of Madness]]'', was released on June 24, 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r1390177|pure_url=yes}} |title=The Sound of Madness – Allmusic review |first=Stephen Thomas |last=Erlewine |publisher=[[Rovi Corporation]] |access-date=February 3, 2011 }}</ref> It debuted at number eight on the ''Billboard'' 200 top album charts, selling 50,000 copies in its opening week.<ref name="LoudSales">{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-rack-up-best-week-ever-on-billboard-charts-with-amaryllis/|title=Shinedown Rack Up Best Week Ever on Billboard Charts With 'Amaryllis'|website=Loudwire|date=April 5, 2012 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> In order to start touring in support of the album, Smith assembled a new official lineup for the band, consisting of [[Nick Perri]] of [[Silvertide]] on lead guitar, Eric Bass on bass guitar, and upgrading touring member, Zach Myers to a permanent rhythm guitarist position.<ref name="SPInterview"/> Perri toured only briefly with the band in 2008, before leaving to pursue a solo career, a move Smith was fine with, as he felt the band operated better as a quartet, leaving Myers as the primary guitarist.<ref name="SPInterview"/>

Through multiple successful single releases, and extensive touring, the album ended up being the band's best-selling, staying on the ''Billboard'' 200 charts for 120 consecutive weeks, and eventually being certified double platinum in the United States, indicating two million units sold.<ref name="Billboard2012">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/499358/shinedown-get-harder-better-faster-stronger-on-amaryllis|title=Shinedown Get Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger on 'Amaryllis'|website=Billboard.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref><ref name="RIAAcert">{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=Shinedown&ti=&col=format&ord=asc#search_section|title=Gold & Platinum - RIAA|website=RIAA.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Six singles were released from the album: "[[Devour (song)|Devour]]", "[[Second Chance (Shinedown song)|Second Chance]]", "[[Sound of Madness]]", "[[If You Only Knew (Shinedown song)|If You Only Knew]]", "[[The Crow & the Butterfly]]", and "[[Diamond Eyes (Boom-Lay Boom-Lay Boom)]]"; each one topping a Billboard rock music chart.<ref name="Billboard2012"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-bassist-interviewed-on-103-9-the-x-video/|title=Shinedwon Bassist Interviewed On 103.9 THE X (Video)|date=May 21, 2012|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref><ref name="NC2012"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/06/28/shinedown-the-sound-of-madness-review |title=Shinedown – The Sound of Madness Review |first=Ed |last=Thompson |date=June 28, 2008 |publisher=IGN |access-date=February 3, 2011 }}</ref> Of particular note was "Second Chance", which crossed over to the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number 7, and eventually being certified triple platinum, indicating three million units of the single sold.<ref name="Hot100"/><ref name="RIAAcert"/>

The band, with its new lineup, once again toured extensively in support of the album release, spending over two years on live performances.<ref name="Billboard2012"/> Of note, the band headlined the "[[Carnival of Madness]]" tour, which involved larger, 10,000 capacity arena venues, and a later "Anything and Everything Tour," which involved acoustic performances in smaller venues and Q&A (question and answer) sessions with the crowd.<ref name="Billboard2012"/> ''[[Somewhere in the Stratosphere]]'', a live album/DVD, was released in May 2011, documenting performances from both tours.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-more-somewhere-in-the-stratosphere-details-revealed/|title=Shinedown: More 'Somewhere In The Stratosphere' Details Revealed|date=April 12, 2011|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>

===2011–2014: ''Amaryllis''===
[[File:Shinedown 2012.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Shinedown in 2012]]
Work on a fourth studio album began in February 2011, with the band spending the first half of the year writing and demoing over 33 songs.<ref name="Billboard2012"/> The band again decided to work with Cavallo as a producer, but moved into a new sound and lyrical direction on the album, capturing a more of a message of  "empowerment, perseverance, and inspiration", inspired by Smith's then-recent change of getting sober and living a healthier lifestyle, and the new band members contributing to the writing process for the first time on an album.<ref name="LATimesSmith">{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/health/la-xpm-2013-jan-12-la-he-five-questions-smith-20130112-story.html|title=Brent Smith of Shinedown cleans up and slims down|first=James|last=Fell|date=January 12, 2013|newspaper=LA Times}}</ref><ref name="Billboard2012"/><ref name="NC2012">{{cite web|url=http://noisecreep.com/shinedown-amaryllis/|title=Shinedown Announce New Album: 'Amaryllis' Will Hit Stores in March|website=Noisecreep|date=January 3, 2012 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> The recording process wrapped up about a year later in February 2012, and the album, ''[[Amaryllis (Shinedown album)|Amaryllis]],'' was released the next month, on March 27, 2012, in 30 countries simultaneously, through a joint release between Atlantic and [[Roadrunner Records]] in countries Atlantic did not distribute into.<ref name="Billboard2012"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gibson.com/News-Lifestyle/Features/en-us/Top-10-Rock-Metal-and-Alternative-Albums-of-2012.aspx|title=Top 10 Rock, Metal and Alternative Albums of 2012|access-date=March 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328015600/http://www.gibson.com/News-Lifestyle/Features/en-us/Top-10-Rock-Metal-and-Alternative-Albums-of-2012.aspx|archive-date=March 28, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{AllMusic |class=album |id=r2401877 |tab=review |label=Shinedown: ''Amaryllis''  Review |first=Gregory |last=Heaney |access-date=March 28, 2012}}</ref> ''Amaryllis'' debuted at number four on the ''Billboard 200'' charts, selling 106,000 copies in its opening week.<ref name="LoudSales"/> While the opening sales doubled the debut of ''The Sound of Madness'', overall sales fell well short, with the album only being certified Gold, indicating a half million copies sold.<ref name="LoudSales"/><ref name="RIAAcert"/>

Five singles were released from the album: "[[Bully (song)|Bully]]", "[[Unity (Shinedown song)|Unity]]", "[[Enemies (Shinedown song)|Enemies]]", "[[I'll Follow You (Shinedown song)|I'll Follow You]]", and "[[Adrenaline (Shinedown song)|Adrenaline]]".<ref name="Loud2013">{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-adrenaline-video/|title=Shinedown Unveil 'Adrenaline' Video|website=Loudwire|date=October 29, 2013 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Steve Baltin |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/shinedown-top-the-charts-stand-up-to-bullies-20120405 |title=Shinedown Top the Charts, Stand Up to Bullies &#124; Music News |publisher=Rolling Stone |date=2012-04-05 |access-date=2014-02-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://mindequalsblown.net/2012/03/27/amaryllis-shinedown/ |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120331081434/http://mindequalsblown.net/2012/03/27/amaryllis-shinedown/ |url-status= usurped |archive-date= March 31, 2012 |title=Shinedown: Amaryllis &#124; Mind Equals Blown |first=Tim |last=Dodderidge |work= at mindequalsblown.net |access-date=March 28, 2012}}</ref> The band's singles once again fared well, albeit it slightly below ''The Sound of Madness'' singles; "Bully" and "Unity" topped the ''Billboard'' Mainstream Rock Charts, "Enemies" and "I'll Follow You" peaked at number 2, and "Adrenaline" peaked at number 4.<ref name="Chartpg1"/> Additionally, only "Bully" managed to have any cross-over success, breaking into the ''Billboard'' Top 100 chart at number 94<ref name="Hot100"/> and eventually being certified Gold as well.<ref name="RIAAcert"/> Shinedown also contributed the non-album song titled "I'm Alive" to the soundtrack of the 2012 film ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|The Avengers]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-five-finger-death-punch-evanescence-featured-on-avengers-assemble-soundtrack/|title=Shinedown, Five Finger Death Punch, Evanescence Featured On 'Avengers Assemble' Soundtrack|date=March 27, 2012|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>
[[File:Zach Myers of Shinedown at the Dow Event Center, February 2013.jpg|thumb|Zach Myers performing in 2013]]
In November 2012, Smith announced in an [[NME]] interview that a follow up Shinedown album had already been recorded.<ref name="Loud2014">{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/brent-smith-upcoming-album-strongest-shinedown-record/|title=Brent Smith: Upcoming Album Is 'Strongest Shinedown Record'|website=Loudwire|date=July 6, 2015 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Smith stated "We have another record of material. It's actually recorded...It's still very massive, it still has an epic feel to it all, but the tempo is a little slower, and the subject matter is a little different. I would say it's actually a bit darker, a little bit more mischievous."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/nme-video/shinedown---we-have-a-new-record-recorded-world-exclusive/1952831048001 |title=Shinedown - 'We Have A New Record Recorded' (World Exclusive) video |publisher=NME.com|date=November 7, 2012|access-date=November 7, 2012}}</ref><ref name="Loud20122nd">{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/brent-smith-upcoming-album-strongest-shinedown-record/|title=Brent Smith: Upcoming Album Is 'Strongest Shinedown Record'|website=Loudwire|date=July 6, 2015 |access-date=May 8, 2018}}</ref> Despite the announcement, the band proceeded to continue on with the ''Amaryllis'' touring cycle, touring through 2013 to complete another two year touring cycle.<ref name="Loud2013"/> Shinedown and [[Three Days Grace]] embarked on a co-headlined tour beginning in February 2013,<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/474222/shinedown-three-days-grace-unite-for-arena-tour | title=Shinedown, Three Days Grace Unite for Arena Tour | magazine=Billboard.com | date=November 12, 2012 | access-date=December 3, 2012}}</ref> and went on another iteration of the yearly "Carnival of Madness" tour with [[Papa Roach]] in later 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/2013-carnival-of-madness-initial-dates/|title=2013 Carnival of Madness Unveils Initial Dates|website=Loudwire|date=June 3, 2013 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>

In April 2013, Smith and Myers recorded ten acoustic [[cover song]]s, selected out of a pool of over 4,000 fan requests, selecting a variety of different types of songs, from [[Metallica]]'s "[[Nothing Else Matters]]" to [[Adele]]'s "[[Someone like You (Adele song)|Someone Like You]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-brent-smith-carnival-of-madness-next-album-rise-of-rock-n-roll/ |title=Shinedown's Brent Smith Talks Carnival of Madness, Next Album + Rise of Rock 'N' Roll |publisher=Loudwire.com |date=June 4, 2013 |access-date=November 18, 2013}}</ref><ref name="BBAcousticEP"/> The tracks were released across two separate EPs, ''[[Acoustic Sessions (Shinedown EP)|Acoustic Sessions]]'' on January 28, 2014,  and ''Acoustic Sessions Pt. 2'' on March 28, 2014, with performance videos created for every track on the first EP.<ref name="BBAcousticEP">{{cite magazine | url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/5877059/shinedown-smith-myers-acoustic-ep-video-premiere-london-calling | title=The duo recorded acoustic versions of classic songs for an EP due out Jan. 28; Watch the premiere of The Clash's "London Calling" | magazine=Billboard.com | date=January 21, 2014 | access-date=April 30, 2014 | author=Graff, Gary}}</ref> The band took much of 2014 off, a rarity for the band, which had pretty consistently moved back and forth between recording and touring for each album cycle.<ref name="Loud2014"/> The time off was for the band to rest, specifically Smith, who had damaged his [[vocal cords]] and contracted [[oral thrush]] from the constant years of touring prior.<ref name="Loud2014"/>

===2015–2016: ''Threat to Survival''===
[[File:2016 RiP Shinedown - Eric Bass - by 2eight - DSC8685.jpg|thumb|150px|Eric Bass performing in 2016]]
Recording for the band's fifth studio album began in January 2015, with a goal of a July or August release date.<ref name="LWFeb2015">{{cite magazine | last=Childers| first=Chad| title =Brent Smith Reveals Timeline for New Shinedown Album + Single| magazine =Loudwire| date =February 20, 2015| url =http://loudwire.com/brent-smith-timeline-new-shinedown-album-single/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> The band later embarked on a summer headlining tour with [[Nothing More]].<ref name="LWApr2015">{{cite magazine | last=Zadrozny| first=Anya| title =Shinedown Announce Summer U.S. Tour Dates + Confirm 2015 Album Release| magazine =Loudwire| date =April 13, 2015| url =http://loudwire.com/shinedown-summer-tour-dates-2015-album-release/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> The first single from the album, "[[Cut the Cord]]" was released in June 2015, ahead of the album's release.<ref name="BBJun2015">{{cite magazine | last=Payne| first=Chris| title =Shinedown Premieres 'Cut the Cord' Video -- First New Song in Three Years| magazine =Billboard| date =June 29, 2015| url =https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/shinedown-cut-cord-video-new-song-brent-smith-exclusive-premiere-2015-6612983/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref><ref name="BBAug2015">{{cite magazine | last=Payne| first=Chris| title =Shinedown & Breaking Benjamin Announce Co-Headlining Fall Dates| magazine =Billboard| date =August 20, 2015| url =https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/shinedown-breaking-benjamin-2015-tour-dates-6656811/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> Two more promotional songs were released in August as well, "Black Cadillac"<ref name="LWBC">{{cite magazine | last=Childers| first=Chad| title =Shinedown Release Soulful New Song 'Black Cadillac'| magazine =Loudwire| date =August 14, 2015| url =http://loudwire.com/shinedown-new-song-black-cadillac/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> and "[[State of My Head]]".<ref name="USA2015">{{cite news | last=Mansfield| first=Brian| title =Shinedown premieres 'State of My Head'|newspaper =USA Today| date =August 27, 2015| url =https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/music/2015/08/27/shinedown-state-of-my-head-premiere/32407895/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref>

In August 2015, the band announced the name of the album, ''[[Threat to Survival]]'', and its release date of September 18, 2015.<ref name="LWAug2015">{{cite magazine | last=Kaufman| first=Spencer| title =Shinedown Announce New Album 'Threat to Survival'| magazine =Loudwire| date =August 7, 2015| url =http://loudwire.com/shinedown-new-album-threat-to-survival/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> The album debuted at number six on the ''Billboard'' 200, selling 65,000 in the first week, lower than their prior album, ''Amaryllis.''<ref name="BBSep2015">{{cite magazine | last=Caulfield| first=Keith| title =Seven Debuts Hit Top 10 of Billboard 200 Chart, Led by Drake & Future, Lana Del Rey and Mac Miller| magazine =Billboard| date =September 27, 2015| url =https://www.billboard.com/pro/billboard-200-top-10-debuts-drake-future-lana-del-rey-mac-miller/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedowns-threat-to-survival-misses-top-five-in-billboard-chart-debut/|title=Shinedown's 'Threat To Survival' Misses Top Five In Billboard Chart Debut|date=September 29, 2015|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Despite the drop in sales, the band still found success in their singles. Four singles were released from the album, and three of the four singles - "Cut the Cord,", "State of My Head", and "[[How Did You Love]]" hit number one on the US Mainstream Rock charts,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-how-did-you-love-tops-billboards-mainstream-rock-songs-chart/|title=Shinedown's 'How Did You Love' Tops Billboard's Mainstream Rock Songs Chart|date=February 24, 2017|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> while the other, "[[Asking for It (Shinedown song)|Asking for It]]", peaked at number two.<ref name="Chartpg1"/> After the album's release, they embarked on a co-headlining US tour with [[Breaking Benjamin]] that would take place between October and November 2015.<ref name="BBAug2015"/> The tour went on to gross a total of $5.7 million.<ref name="BBDec2015">{{cite magazine | last=Allen| first=Bob| title =Shinedown & Breaking Benjamin Wrap Fall Trek, Lead Hot Tours| magazine =Billboard| date =December 2, 2015| url =https://www.billboard.com/pro/shinedown-breaking-benjamin-hot-tours/| access-date =May 29, 2018}}</ref> 
[[File:2016 RiP Shinedown - Barry Kerch - by 2eight - DSC8938.jpg|thumb|left|Barry Kerch performing in 2016]]
The band continued touring in 2016, headlining U.S. dates with [[The Virginmarys]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/shinedown-march-2016-tour-the-virginmarys/|title=Shinedown Reveal 2016 Tour Dates With The Virginmarys|date=December 14, 2015|website=Loudwire|access-date=October 5, 2020}}</ref> The group appeared on ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live]]'' in April 2016, and, the following month, they performed at several festivals including the Fort Rock Festival<ref name="LWKimmel">{{cite magazine | last=Divita| first=Joe| title =Shinedown to Perform on 'Jimmy Kimmel Live'| magazine =Loudwire| date =April 16, 2016| url =http://loudwire.com/shinedown-perform-jimmy-kimmel-live/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref><ref name="NH">{{cite news| last =Spencer| first =Robbie| title =From Jimmy Kimmel to Fort Rock: Shinedown Headlines Fort Rock 2016| newspaper =Naples Herald| date =May 2, 2016| url =http://naplesherald.com/2016/05/01/jimmy-kimmel-fort-rock-shinedown-closes-fort-rock-2016/| access-date =May 30, 2018| archive-date =August 4, 2018| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20180804014039/http://naplesherald.com/2016/05/01/jimmy-kimmel-fort-rock-shinedown-closes-fort-rock-2016/| url-status =dead}}</ref> and Rock'N Derby.<ref name="LWDerby">{{cite magazine | last=Ramanand| first=Liz| title =Rock'N Derby 2016: Day 3 – Sevendust, Megadeth, Shinedown, Ghost + More| magazine =Loudwire| date =May 31, 2016| url =http://loudwire.com/rockn-derby-2016-day-3-sevendust-megadeth-shinedown-ghost-more/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> The band also headlined the 2016 version of the Carnival of Madness tour with [[Halestorm]] in July and August.<ref name="LWCarnival">{{cite magazine | last=Childers| first=Chad| title =Shinedown To Headline 2016 Carnival of Madness With Halestorm, Black Stone Cherry + More| magazine =Loudwire| date =March 14, 2016| url =http://loudwire.com/shinedown-headline-2016-carnival-of-madness-halestorm-black-stone-cherry-more/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref><ref name="LWCarnival2016">{{cite magazine | last=Ramanand| first=Liz| title =Shinedown Bring Carnival of Madness to Coney Island in Brooklyn With Halestorm + More| magazine =Loudwire| date =August 10, 2016| url =http://loudwire.com/shinedown-carnival-of-madness-coney-island-2016-recap-photo-gallery/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> Later in 2016, the band went on a fall U.S. arena tour with [[Sixx AM]] and [[Five Finger Death Punch]] that was extended into December.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/sixxam-tour-recap-video-7655066/|title=Watch Tour Recap Reel From Sixx:A.M.: Exclusive|website=Billboard.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref><ref name="AI2016Tour">{{cite news | last=Erickson| first=Anne| title =Shinedown and Five Finger Death Punch Extend Fall Tour| publisher =Audio Ink Radio| date =August 25, 2016| url =http://audioinkradio.com/2016/08/shinedown-five-finger-death-punch-extend-fall-tour/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref>

===2017–2020: ''Attention Attention''===
In February 2017, Smith announced that they had begun work on a sixth studio album.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-22-pieces-written-possible-first-concept-album/|title=Shinedown Have Potential Concept Album in the Works|website=Loudwire|date=February 9, 2017 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Bass had been working on writing 22 separate pieces of music over the course of their 2016 touring, separate from the rest of the band, who wanted to just concentrate on touring.<ref name="B221">{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-is-working-on-possible-concept-album-says-brent-smith/|title=Shinedown Is Working On Possible Concept Album, Says Brent Smith|date=February 8, 2017|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Bass had just begun presenting the material to Smith, who, while unsure how much exactly would go into the future album, did say that he was very impressed, and that the material may fit together into a [[concept album]], a first for the band.<ref name="B221"/> They joined [[Iron Maiden]] on tour in Europe in April and May, and began recording soon after.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=23458|title=Iron Maiden Set To Hit The Stages On The European The Book Of Souls 2017 Tour.|publisher=knac}}</ref> At the time, the band planned to finish the album in late 2017, release a first single in January 2018, and then release the album in April.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-spring-2018-album-first-single-january/|title=Shinedown Announce Plans for New Album and Single for 2018|website=Loudwire|date=July 13, 2017 |access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> In January 2018, Myers announced that the band had finished recording the album, and that Bass was working on finalizing the production and [[audio mixing|mixing]] of the album.<ref name="Blab118"/> Myers also described the album's sound as "heavier than ''Threat to Survival''."<ref name="Blab118">{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-completes-recording-new-album-its-heavier-than-threat-to-survival-says-zach-myers/|title=Shinedown Completes Recording New Album: 'It's Heavier Than ''Threat To Survival'',' Says Zach Myers|date=January 7, 2018|website=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=May 8, 2018}}</ref>

On March 7, 2018, the band announced the album's title, ''[[Attention Attention]]'', and released its first single, "[[Devil (Shinedown song)|Devil]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://teamrock.com/news/2018-03-07/shinedown-announce-new-album-release-video-for-devil-single|title=Shinedown announce new album, release video for Devil single|website=Teamrock.com|date=March 7, 2018 |access-date=May 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kerrang.com/video/shinedown-have-released-new-single-video-devil/|title=Shinedown Have Released A New Single And Video, Devil — Kerrang!|website=Kerrang!|date=March 7, 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-to-release-attention-attention-album-in-may-devil-video-available/|title=Shineown To Release 'Attention Attention' Album In May; 'Devil' Video Available|date=March 7, 2018|publisher=Blabbermouth}}</ref> "Devil" would eventually reach number 1 on the [[Active rock|Active Rock]] and Mainstream Rock charts.<ref name="Chartpg1"/><ref name="Parade2018">{{cite news | last=Whitmore| first=Laura B.| title =Shinedown Release New Album Attention Attention| publisher =Parade| date =May 4, 2018| url =https://parade.com/667810/laurawhitmore/shinedown-release-new-album-attention-attention/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> ''Attention Attention'' was released on May 4, 2018, and was Shinedown's first album to be produced and mixed entirely by a member of the band (Eric Bass).<ref name="Parade2018"/> The album debuted at number 1 on the Top Rock Albums, Hard Rock Albums, and Alternative Albums charts. It was the second time the band had achieved that feat (''Amaryllis'' also topped all three charts). It has thus far peaked at number 5 on the ''Billboard'' 200 chart, selling 61,000 units in the process.<ref name="BBMay2018">{{cite magazine | last=Rutherford| first=Kevin| title =Shinedown Commands 'Attention' Atop Rock Album Charts| magazine =Billboard| date =May 18, 2018| url =https://www.billboard.com/pro/shinedown-attention-attention-rock-album-charts/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> On April 5, a second song, "The Human Radio" was released as a promotional single, accompanied by a music video.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/video-premiere-shinedowns-the-human-radio/ |title=Video Premiere: Shinedown's 'The Human Radio' |website=Blabbermouth.net |date=April 6, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018}}</ref>
[[File:20180603 Nürnberg Rock im Park Shinedown 0141.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Brent Smith performing in 2018]]
Shortly after the album's release, the band went on a brief co-headlining tour with Five Finger Death Punch.<ref name="Louder">{{cite news | last=Munro| first=Scott| title =Shinedown reflect on new album in studio documentary| publisher =Louder| date =May 9, 2018| url =https://www.loudersound.com/news/shinedown-reflect-on-new-album-in-studio-documentary| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref><ref name="Roanoke2018">{{cite news | last=Dickens| first=Tad| title =Five Finger Death Punch, Shinedown fill Salem Civic Center on a Monday |newspaper =Roanoke Times| date =May 15, 2018| url =http://www.roanoke.com/arts_and_entertainment/music/five-finger-death-punch-shinedown-fill-salem-civic-center-on/article_7e55b796-5800-11e8-a914-bbe58296c8f3.html| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> They also released a 14-minute behind the scenes documentary video about the making of ''Attention Attention''.<ref name="Louder"/><ref name="Roanoke2018"/> The band embarked on a summer co-headlining tour with [[Godsmack]] that began in July 2018.<ref name="Salute">{{cite news | last=Leep| first=Joshua| title =Godsmack and Shinedown announce co-headlining tour| publisher =Salute| date =March 20, 2018| url =https://salutemag.com/2018/03/20/godsmack-shinedown-tour/| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref>

In October 2018, Shinedown announced plans to headline a U.S. tour beginning February 20, 2019, in [[Estero, Florida]].<ref name="Estero tour">{{Cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-announces-u-s-tour-with-papa-roach-asking-alexandria.html|title=Shinedown Announces U.S. Tour With Papa Roach, Asking Alexandria|date=2018-10-01|work=Blabbermouth.net|access-date=October 1, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Supporting acts for the trek included [[Papa Roach]] and [[Asking Alexandria]].<ref name="Estero tour"/> The tour concluded on March 20, 2019, in [[Loveland, Colorado|Loveland, CO]].<ref name="Estero tour"/>

In November 2018, Shinedown regained sole possession of the most top 10 chart placements in the history of Billboard's Rock Airplay chart, with "[[Get Up (Shinedown song)|Get Up]]" the second single from ''Attention Attention''.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/shinedown/chart-history/ark/|title=Shinedown Billboardrocksongs|magazine=Billboard|access-date=March 30, 2019|language=en-US}}</ref> The song earned 5.9 million rock radio audience impressions, a boost of 5 percent, in the week ending Nov. 18, according to Nielsen Music.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/shinedown-breaks-record-most-rock-airplay-top-10s/|title=Shinedown Breaks Record For Most Rock Airplay Top 10s With 'Get Up'|magazine=Billboard|access-date=2019-03-26}}</ref> On March 1, 2019, the band released the song "[[Monsters (Shinedown song)|Monsters]]" as the third single from ''Attention Attention'' and was followed by a music video.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/three-days-grace-mainstream-rock-songs-number-1-record-shinedown-top-10/|title=Three Days Grace Extends Mainstream Rock Songs No. 1 Record, Shinedown Snags 25th Top 10|magazine=Billboard}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://waaf.radio.com/blogs/anthony-capobianco/shinedown-drops-official-video-monsters|title=Shinedown Drops Official Video For "Monsters"|date=June 12, 2019|website=WAAF 107.3 FM|access-date=October 6, 2020|archive-date=February 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200223003621/https://waaf.radio.com/blogs/anthony-capobianco/shinedown-drops-official-video-monsters|url-status=dead}}</ref>  On July 2, 2019, an animated video for the song was also released.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.therockstationz93.com/2019/07/03/shinedown-releases-animated-music-video-for-monsters/|title=Shinedown Releases Animated Music Video for 'Monsters'|date=July 3, 2019|website=Z93 &#124; WKQZ-FM}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|first=Kirsten|last=Spruch|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/shinedown-monsters-video-8518221/|title=Shinedown Explores Their Inner Demons in Animated 'Monsters' Video: Exclusive|magazine=Billboard|date=July 2, 2019|access-date=October 5, 2020}}</ref> On September 24, 2019, the band released the song "[[Attention Attention (Shinedown song)|Attention Attention]]" as the fourth single from ''Attention Attention'' and was followed by a music video.<ref>{{cite web|first=Oleva|last=Berard|url=https://substreammagazine.com/2019/09/shinedown-attention-attention-music-video/|title=Shinedown shares music video for new single "Attention Attention"|date=September 24, 2019|website=Substream Magazine|access-date=October 5, 2020}}</ref>

On March 23, 2020, the band released a previously unreleased song recorded for ''[[Amaryllis (Shinedown album)|Amaryllis]]'' titled "[[Atlas Falls]]", to raise money for [[Direct Relief]] to provide equipment for frontline workers during the 2020 [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Atlas Falls">{{Cite web|url=https://www.axs.com/shinedown-releases-new-song-atlas-falls-to-benefit-direct-relief-138953|title=Official Tickets and Your Source for Live Entertainment &#124; AXS.com|website=www.axs.com}}</ref> The song was available to download with the purchase of a T-shirt.<ref name="Atlas Falls"/> The band donated $20,000 themselves, and raised over $70,000 in the first 36 hours.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=10159493231422589&id=20415872588|title=Shinedown|website=www.facebook.com}}</ref> On May 22, after raising over $300,000, "Atlas Falls" was officially released to streaming services and digital retailers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://loudwire.com/shinedown-atlas-falls/|title=Shinedown Song Hits Streaming After Raising $300K for Charity|website=Loudwire|date=May 22, 2020 }}</ref> On the June 27 tally, "Atlas Falls" became Shinedown's 27th top 10 single on the [[Mainstream Rock Chart]].<ref name="Tom Petty">{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/shinedown-one-away-from-tying-tom-petty-mainstream-rock-songs-top-10s-record|title=Shinedown Now One Away From Tom Petty's Record for Most Mainstream Rock Songs Top 10s|date=June 25, 2020|website=www.billboard.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|date=2020-08-17|title=Shinedown Breaks Record for Most Mainstream Rock Songs No. 1s With 'Atlas Falls'|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/business/chart-beat/9435712/shinedown-mainstream-rock-songs-no-1-record-atlas-falls|access-date=2020-08-20|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> Only Tom Petty has more, with 28.<ref name="Tom Petty"/>

On May 26, 2020, the band announced that they had postponed all of their 2020 summer Deep Dive tour due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], with many dates being rescheduled.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.shinedown.com/|title=Deep Dive Tour Rescheduled - Official Website of Shinedown Official Blog|website=Official Website of Shinedown Official Website}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kwqc.com/content/news/Shinedown-announces-tour-cancellation--affects-Mississippi-Valley-Fair-stop-570778021.html|title=Shinedown announces tour cancellation; affects Mississippi Valley Fair stop|author=KWQC Staff|website=kwqc|date=May 26, 2020 }}</ref>

===2021–2024: ''Planet Zero''===
[[File:ShinedownStAugustine01.jpg|thumb|left|Shinedown performing in [[St. Augustine, Florida]], on October 8, 2021]]
In February 2021, Smith announced that the band had started working on a seventh studio album, with the goal of releasing it in the second half of 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedowns-seventh-album-to-be-released-after-the-summer/|title=Shinedown's Seventh Album To Be Released After The Summer|date=February 21, 2021|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=March 10, 2021}}</ref> The band released a film for their sixth album, ''Attention Attention''. The film was directed by Bill Yukich and was released on September 3, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/shinedown-attention-attention-film-vod-screening/|title=Shinedown's Cinematic 'Attention Attention' Film Heads to VOD|date=July 20, 2021|website=[[Loudwire]]|access-date=August 6, 2021}}</ref> On August 28, 2021, Smith announced the band's first single off the upcoming album is expected to be out in January 2022, with the album following a few months later.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://loudwire.com/shinedown-2022-timeline-new-music/ |title = Shinedown Reveal 2022 Timeline for New Music| website=[[Loudwire]] | date=August 28, 2021 }}</ref>

[[File:Shinedown_at_Mohegan_Sun.jpg|thumb|Shinedown performing in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]], on April 16, 2022]]
On January 26, 2022, the band released the lead single, "[[Planet Zero (song)|Planet Zero]]", from their seventh studio album of the same name. The album was originally set to be released on April 22, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Brannigan|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/shinedown-tease-new-album-planet-zero-with-the-release-of-its-title-track|title=Shinedown tease new album Planet Zero with the release of its title track|website=Louder Sound|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gary|last=Graff|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/shinedown-planet-zero-new-album-interview-1235023021/|title=Shinedown on Dystopian 'Planet Zero' Album: 'This One Tried to Kill Me a Couple Times'|magazine=Billboard|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> On March 25, 2022, the band released a second song, "The Saints of Violence and Innuendo".<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/shinedown-saints-of-violence-and-innuendo-lyric-video/|title=Shinedown Call Out Groupthink + False Narratives in New Song 'The Saints of Violence and Innuendo'|website=Loudwire|date=March 25, 2022|access-date=March 25, 2022}}</ref> On April 12, 2022, the band announced that the album's release was being pushed back to July 1, 2022.<ref name="Delay">{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedowns-planet-zero-pushed-back-to-july/|title=Shinedown's 'Planet Zero' Pushed Back To July|website=Blabbermouth.net|date=April 12, 2022|access-date=April 12, 2022}}</ref> The change was due to a delay in vinyl production, and the band's desire for the fanbase to experience the album simultaneously across formats.<ref name="Delay"/> In April 2022, the band was inducted into "Mohegan Sun's Walk Of Fame".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-to-be-inducted-into-mohegan-suns-walk-of-fame/|title=Shinedown To Be Inducted Into Mohegan Sun's Walk Of Fame|website=Blabbermouth.net|date=April 12, 2022|access-date=April 12, 2022}}</ref> On June 1, 2022, the band released the second single, "[[Daylight (Shinedown song)|Daylight]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-releases-soaring-new-anthem-daylight|title=Shinedown Releases Soaring New Anthem 'Daylight'|website=Blabbermouth.net|date=June 1, 2022|access-date=June 1, 2022}}</ref> After the album's release, "Dead Don't Die" was released as the third single on January 17, 2023, and then "[[A Symptom of Being Human]]" as the fourth on February 22, 2023. "A Symptom of Being Human" was the first Shinedown single since their debut to initially not be released to rock radio, instead debuting on [[Hot Adult Contemporary]] radio and crossing to rock radio later on.<ref>{{Cite magazine|date=June 23, 2023|title=Shinedown Score a Mainstream Hit with 'A Symptom of Being Human': 'It's a Song About Taking a Breath' (Exclusive)|url=https://people.com/shinedown-symptom-of-being-human-exclusive-interview-7552486|last=Despres|first=Tricia|access-date=January 13, 2024|website=[[People (magazine)|People]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/shinedown-symptom-of-being-human-number-1-mainstream-rock-airplay-record-1235580840/|title=Shinedown Adds to Mainstream Rock Airplay No. 1 Record With 'A Symptom of Being Human'|last=Rutherford|first=Kevin|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=January 12, 2024|access-date=January 13, 2024}}</ref> A "Pop Remix" of the song was released on June 23, 2023.

In May 2024 the band launched a signature [[hot sauce]] line, with each of the three sauces named after a different song, the first being the "Symptom Chipotle Garlic Sauce" (named after their 2023 single "[[A Symptom of Being Human]]"),<ref>{{cite web|author=Stephen G.|url=https://popculture.com/music/news/shinedown-launches-hot-sauce-line/|title=Shinedown Launches Hot Sauce Line|work=[[Pop Culture Press|Pop Culture]]|date=May 2, 2024|access-date=January 24, 2025}}</ref> followed by "Devour Pineapple Jerk Sauce" (after their 2008 single, "[[Devour (song)|Devour]]"),<ref>{{cite web|first=Brent|last=Porche|url=https://wmmr.com/2024/07/17/shinedown-new-flavor-hot-sauce/|title=Shinedown Add New Flavor to Hot Sauce Line|work=WMMR|date=July 17, 2024|access-date=January 24, 2025}}</ref> and "Attention Attention Mango Habanero Sauce" (after their 2019 single, "[[Attention Attention (song)|Attention Attention]]").<ref>{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Fields|url=https://www.iheart.com/content/2024-08-27-attention-attention-shinedown-turns-up-the-heat-with-new-hot-sauce-flavor/|title=Attention Attention: Shinedown Turns Up The Heat With New Hot Sauce Flavor|work=[[IHeartMedia|iHeart]]|date=August 27, 2024|access-date=January 24, 2025}}</ref>

===2025–present: Upcoming eighth studio album===
In February 2024, Smith announced that the band was working on its eighth studio album.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/shinedowns-brent-smith-weve-been-working-on-new-material-for-a-while|title=Shinedown's Brent Smith: 'We've Been Working On New Material For A While'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 26, 2024|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref> Throughout 2024, both Kerch and Bass shared details about the upcoming album, the process leading to its production, the musical style and the fact that unlike the previous two albums, the next one will not be a concept album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chuck|last=Armstrong|url=https://loudwire.com/shinedown-barry-kerch-new-music-hot-sauce-interview/|title=Shinedown's Barry Kerch Discusses New Music + Band's Hot Sauce|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=June 12, 2024|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/next-shinedown-album-will-be-different-says-barry-kerch|title=Next Shinedown Album Will Be 'Different', Says Barry Kerch|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=February 2, 2025}}</ref>

On January 24, 2025, the band released two singles, "Three Six Five" and "[[Dance, Kid, Dance]]" from their upcoming eighth studio album.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-releases-two-new-singles-three-six-five-and-dance-kid-dance|title=Shinedown Releases Two New Singles, 'Three Six Five' And 'Dance, Kid, Dance'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=January 24, 2025|access-date=January 24, 2025}}</ref> On July 15, 2025, the album's third single, "Killing Fields", was released.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/shinedown-to-release-new-single-killing-fields-on-tuesday|title=Shinedown To Release New Single 'Killing Fields' On Tuesday|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=July 11, 2025|access-date=July 14, 2025}}</ref>

==Musical style and influences==
Shinedown's music has been described as [[hard rock]], [[alternative metal]], [[post-grunge]], [[alternative rock]], [[pop rock]], [[grunge]], [[arena rock]], and [[nu metal]], with [[Pop music|pop]] and [[Southern rock]] influences.{{Efn|

*Southern rock:<ref name="rock.about"/>}} In August 2013, Kerch disagreed with more specialized genre ascribed to the band, stating that "We're just a [[rock 'n' roll]] band" while conceding that each album did have a markedly different rock sound to them by design.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/popmusic/index.ssf/2013/08/ever-evolving_shinedown_is_jus.html |title=Ever-evolving Shinedown is 'just a rock 'n' roll band,' says drummer Barry Kerch |publisher=cleveland.com |date=August 8, 2013 |access-date=December 13, 2013}}</ref> The nu metal label has been applied to the band's earlier work by journalists on occasion,<ref name="ALLMTTS" /> though the band disputes that term as well.<ref name="GuitarPlayer1"/> The band's first album, ''Leave a Whisper'', largely stayed away from having any [[guitar solos]], something then-guitarist Todd felt was undesirable due to the popularity of nu metal at the time of recording the album, though he felt the band was never particularly part of the genre's movement.<ref name="GuitarPlayer1"/> With nu metal falling out of popularity by the mid-2000s, they began adding guitar solos more prominently to their music, starting with their next album, ''Us and Them''.<ref name="GuitarPlayer1">{{cite web|url=http://www.guitarplayer.com/miscellaneous/1139/shinedown39s-jasin-todd-southern-fried-metal/15935|title=Shinedown's Jasin Todd: Southern Fried Metal|first=Electric & Acoustic Guitar Gear, Lessons, News, Blogs, Video, Tabs & Chords -|last=GuitarPlayer.com|website=GuitarPlayer.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> ''Us and Them'' has also been described as less "grungy" than its predecessor with "more twisted, progressive song structures".<ref name="CCP">{{cite news | last=Harris| first=Vincent| title =Shinedown continues down their own heavy-rock path after 15 years |newspaper =Charleston City Paper| date =November 30, 2016| url =https://www.charlestoncitypaper.com/charleston/shinedown-continues-down-their-own-heavy-rock-path-after-15-years/Content?oid=6337097| access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref>

''[[The Sound of Madness]]'' went in different musical and lyrical directions as compared to the band's previous two albums.<ref name="LexGo2013">{{cite news|first=Walter|last=Tunis|url=http://www.kentucky.com/entertainment/music-news-reviews/article44403504.html|title=With time on its side and tumult in its past, Shinedown's goal is career longevity|newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader|date=February 14, 2013|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref><ref name="NewsOK">{{cite news|first=Gene|last=Triplett|url=https://newsok.com/article/3277316/inspiring-woman-leads-shinedown-to-love-song|title=Inspiring woman leads Shinedown to love song|newspaper=The Oklahoman|date =August 1, 2008|access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> Barry Kerch noted that lineup changes and volatility in the band members' lives produced a darker and angrier sound.<ref name="LexGo2013"/><ref name="NewsOK"/> The album's lead single, "[[Devour (song)|Devour]]", is an anti-war anthem, but ''The Sound of Madness'' also contains "[[If You Only Knew (Shinedown song)|If You Only Knew]]", the band's first love ballad.<ref name="LexGo2013"/><ref name="NewsOK"/> ''[[Amaryllis (Shinedown album)|Amaryllis]]'' has been noted to have a more positive, "anthemic" bent.<ref name="AMAmaryllis">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/amaryllis-mw0002307581|title =AllMusic Review by Gregory Heaney|website=AllMusic|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Loudwire]]'', Anne Erickson described the album's sound as "aggressive-yet-cathartic."<ref name="LWAmaryllis">{{cite magazine|first=Anne|last=Erickson|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-amaryllis-album-review/|title =Shinedown, 'Amaryllis' – Album Review|magazine=Loudwire|date=March 26, 2012|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref> Their fifth studio album, ''[[Threat to Survival]]'', was described as the band's most "pop-oriented" album, with the single "[[State of My Head]]" being referred to as "a slick amalgam of electro-pop and vintage alt-rock with a catchy as hell though extremely well-worn chorus."<ref name="AMThreat">{{cite web|first=James Christopher|last=Monger|url =https://www.allmusic.com/album/threat-to-survival-mw0002869886|title =AllMusic Review by James Christopher Monger|website=AllMusic|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref> The 2018 follow-up, ''[[Attention Attention]]'', is a concept album that begins with the narrator in a "dark, negative place" and gradually emerging from that over the course of the track listing.<ref name="BBAttention">{{cite magazine|first=Kevin|last=Rutherford|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/shinedown-attention-attention-album-devil-video-8232518/|title=Shinedown Announces New Album 'Attention Attention,' Releases Single 'Devil': Video Premiere|magazine=Billboard|date=March 7, 2018|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref> Both ''Threat to Survival'' and ''Attention Attention'' have been described as having more of a [[pop rock]] sound but have also been described as hard rock.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Bowar|url=http://loudwire.com/shinedown-threat-to-survival-album-review/|title=Shinedown, 'Threat To Survival' - Album Review|work=Loudwire|date=September 25, 2015|access-date=January 27, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Anne|last=Erickson|url=http://audioinkradio.com/2018/04/shinedown-attention-attention-review/|title=Shinedown Crafts Heavy, Hopeful Rock On 'Attention Attention' – Review|website=Audio Ink Radio|date=April 23, 2018|access-date=July 28, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Wes|last=Derby|url=https://metalnation.com/album-review-shinedown-attention-attention/|title=Album Review: Shinedown – Attention Attention|publisher=Metalnation|date=April 28, 2018|access-date=July 28, 2018}}</ref><ref name="sonicabuse" />

The band has cited [[Stone Temple Pilots]], [[Otis Redding]], [[Pink Floyd]], and [[Iron Maiden]] as influences.<ref name="HeraldDispatch">{{cite news|first=Derek|last=Halsey|url=http://www.herald-dispatch.com/features_entertainment/shinedown-breaking-benjamin-sevendust-bring-hard-rock-to-arena/article_598b10a4-5890-5bea-94fc-d900a80cba12.html|title=Shinedown, Breaking Benjamin, Sevendust bring hard rock to arena|newspaper=The Herald-Dispatch|date=November 21, 2015|access-date =May 30, 2018}}</ref> Primary songwriter, Brent Smith, has also cited [[Etta James]], [[Ella Fitzgerald]], [[The Doors]], [[Soundgarden]], and [[Metallica]] as some of his influences.<ref name="AISmith">{{cite news|first=Ann|last=Ericksone|url=http://audioinkradio.com/2011/02/shinedown-interview-brent-smith|title=Interview: Shinedown Vocalist Inspired by Chris Cornell, Otis Redding|publisher =Audio Ink Radio|date =February 2011|access-date=May 30, 2018}}</ref>

'''Soundgarden''' was an American [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]], in 1984 by singer and drummer [[Chris Cornell]], lead guitarist [[Kim Thayil]], and bassist [[Hiro Yamamoto]]. Cornell switched to rhythm guitar in 1985, replaced on drums initially by Scott Sundquist, and later by [[Matt Cameron]] in 1986. Yamamoto left in 1989 and was replaced initially by [[Jason Everman]] and shortly thereafter by [[Ben Shepherd]]. Soundgarden disbanded in 1997 and reformed in 2010. Following Cornell's death in 2017, Thayil declared in October 2018 that Soundgarden had disbanded a second time. The surviving members of the band have continued to occasionally work together since then, including reuniting for a one-off concert in tribute to Cornell in January 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.93x.com/2019/01/22/watch-soundgardens-complete-chris-cornell-tribute-set/|title=Watch Soundgarden's Complete Chris Cornell Tribute Set|website=[[KXXR|93X]]|date=January 22, 2019|access-date=July 19, 2022}}</ref> and again in December 2024 for a benefit concert in Seattle with Shaina Shepherd on vocals under the [[anagram]] '''Nudedragons'''.<ref name="nudedragons24">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.revolvermag.com/events/soundgarden-members-to-reunite-for-benefit-show-with-shaina-shepherd-on-vocals/ |title=SOUNDGARDEN members to reunite for benefit show with SHAINA SHEPHERD on vocals |date=December 4, 2024 |magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]}}</ref>

Soundgarden was one of the pioneers of [[grunge]] music, a style of [[alternative rock]] that developed in the American [[Pacific Northwest]] in the mid-1980s, and helped to popularize it in the early 1990s, alongside such Seattle contemporaries as [[Alice in Chains]], [[Pearl Jam]], and [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]]. They were the first of a number of grunge bands to sign to the Seattle-based record label [[Sub Pop]], through which they released two [[Extended play|EP]]s: ''[[Screaming Life]]'' (1987) and ''[[Fopp (EP)|Fopp]]'' (1988). Soundgarden's debut album, ''[[Ultramega OK]]'', was also released in 1988 by the [[Los Angeles]]-based independent label [[SST Records]]; although the album did not sell well nationally, it garnered critical acclaim and the band's first [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] nomination. Soundgarden was the first grunge band to be signed to a major label when they signed to [[A&M Records]] in 1988. The release of their second album, ''[[Louder Than Love]]'' (1989), was the band's first album to enter the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] chart, peaking at number 108, and spawned two radio hits: "[[Hands All Over (Soundgarden song)|Hands All Over]]" and "[[Loud Love]]".

Soundgarden's third album ''[[Badmotorfinger]]'' (1991) helped usher in the mainstream success of grunge. The album was buoyed by the success of the singles "[[Jesus Christ Pose]]", "[[Outshined]]", and "[[Rusty Cage]]", reached number 39 on the ''Billboard'' 200 and has been certified [[RIAA certification|double-platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). The band's fourth album, ''[[Superunknown]]'' (1994), expanded their popularity; it debuted at number one on the ''Billboard'' 200 and yielded the Grammy Award-winning singles "[[Spoonman]]" and "[[Black Hole Sun]]". Soundgarden experimented with new sonic textures on their follow-up album ''[[Down on the Upside]]'' (1996), which debuted at number two on the ''Billboard'' 200 and spawned several hit singles of its own, including "[[Pretty Noose]]", "[[Burden in My Hand]]", and "[[Blow Up the Outside World]]". In 1997, the band broke up due to internal strife over its creative direction and exhaustion from touring. After more than a decade of working on projects and other bands, they reunited in 2010. [[Republic Records]] released their sixth and final studio album, ''[[King Animal]]'', in 2012.

By 2019, Soundgarden had sold more than 14 million records in the United States<ref name="riaa">{{cite web|url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&artist=Soundgarden&startMonth=1&endMonth=1&startYear=1958&endYear=2008&sort=Artist&perPage=25|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120526210337/http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&artist=Soundgarden&startMonth=1&endMonth=1&startYear=1958&endYear=2008&sort=Artist&perPage=25 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 26, 2012 |title=Gold and Platinum Database Search  |work=[[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]]  |access-date=February 12, 2007}}</ref> and an estimated 30 million worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vh1.com/artists/news/502068/09251998/soundgarden.jhtml |title=Ex-Soundgarden Singer Chris Cornell Plows Ahead With Solo Debut |date=September 25, 1998 |access-date=January 19, 2008 |author=Kaufman, Gil |publisher=[[VH1|VH1.com]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090905000455/http://www.vh1.com/artists/news/502068/09251998/soundgarden.jhtml |archive-date=September 5, 2009 }}</ref> [[VH1]] ranked them at number 14 in their special, ''100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock'' list.<ref name="vh1 greatest"/> The band was selected for induction into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2025.<ref name="rr25">{{cite web |title=The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Foundation unveils electrifying class of 2025 inductees |url=https://rockhall.com/press-release/the-rock-roll-hall-of-fame-foundation-unveils-electrifying-class-of-2025-inductees/ |website=Rock & Roll Hall of Fame |access-date=28 April 2025}}</ref>

==History==
===Formation and early recordings (1984–1988)===
[[File:Soundgarden live 1985.jpg|thumb|right|Soundgarden in 1985]]
Soundgarden's origin is a band called the Shemps, which performed around Seattle in the early 1980s<ref name="history">{{cite book|last=Anderson|first=Kyle|title=Accidental Revolution|publisher=St. Martin's Griffin|location=New York|year=2007|isbn=978-0-312-35819-8|pages=[https://archive.org/details/accidentalrevolu0000ande/page/112 112–116]|url=https://archive.org/details/accidentalrevolu0000ande/page/112}}</ref> and included bassist [[Hiro Yamamoto]] and drummer and singer [[Chris Cornell]]. Following Yamamoto's departure, the band recruited guitarist [[Kim Thayil]] as its new bassist.<ref name="history"/> Thayil moved to Seattle from [[Park Forest, Illinois]], with Yamamoto and [[Bruce Pavitt]], who later started the independent record label [[Sub Pop]].<ref>[[Jim DeRogatis|DeRogatis, Jim]]. ''Milk It!: Collected Musings on the Alternative Music Explosion of the 90's''. Cambridge: Da Capo, 2003. {{ISBN|0-306-81271-1}}, pg. 69</ref> Cornell and Yamamoto stayed in contact, and after the Shemps broke up Cornell and Yamamoto started [[jam session|jamming]] together, and were eventually joined by Thayil.<ref name="history"/>

Soundgarden was formed in 1984 and included Cornell (drums <!--Cornell started on DRUMS for Soundgarden - please do not change this to "guitar"-->and vocals), Yamamoto (bass), and Thayil (guitar). The band named themselves after a wind-channeling pipe sculpture titled ''[[A Sound Garden]]'',<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Corcoran |first=Michael |date=December 1989 |title=Northwest of Hell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=msdh3F68Q44C&pg=PA42 |magazine=SPIN |pages=42}}</ref> on [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] property at 7600 Sand Point Way, next to [[Magnuson Park (Seattle)|Magnuson Park]] in Seattle.<!-- When the band took their name, there wasn't a distinction between NOAA and Magnuson Park, but the Sound Garden is now fenced away from the park. --><ref>"Nirvana and the Story of Grunge". ''[[Q (magazine)|Q]]''. pg. 102. December 2005.</ref> Cornell originally played drums while singing, but in 1985 the band enlisted Scott Sundquist to allow Cornell to concentrate on vocals.<ref>George-Warren, Holly, Patricia Romanowski, and [[Jon Pareles]]. ''The Rolling Stone Encyclopedia of Rock & Roll''. Rolling Stone Press. 2001. {{ISBN|0-671-43457-8}}.</ref> The band traveled around playing various concerts with this lineup for about a year. Their first recordings were three songs that appeared on the 1986 compilation album for [[C/Z Records]] called ''[[Deep Six (album)|Deep Six]]'': "Heretic", "Tears to Forget" and "All Your Lies".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/deep-six-mw0000113240 |title=Deep Six - Various Artists |website=[[Allmusic]] |access-date=November 1, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228161020/http://www.allmusic.com/album/deep-six-mw0000113240 |archive-date=December 28, 2016 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> It also featured songs by fellow grunge pioneers [[Green River (band)|Green River]], [[Skin Yard]], [[Malfunkshun]], [[the U-Men]], and the [[Melvins]]. In 1986, Cornell's then-girlfriend and future wife, [[Susan Silver]] started managing Soundgarden.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qbr6WdsnLzQC&pg=RA10-PA20 |title=The Age of Innocents |date=September 17, 2011 |magazine=Billboard |page=20}}</ref> In the same year, Sundquist left the band to spend time with his family and was replaced by former Skin Yard drummer [[Matt Cameron]].<ref name="history"/>

[[File:Soundgarden (1987 Sub Pop promo photo).jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.7|Soundgarden in 1987]]
A Soundgarden performance one night impressed [[KEXP-FM|KCMU]] DJ [[Jonathan Poneman]], who later said: "I saw this band that was everything rock music should be."<ref>[[Michael Azerrad|Azerrad, Michael]]. ''[[Our Band Could Be Your Life]]''. Little Brown and Company, 2001. {{ISBN|0-316-78753-1}}, pg. 422</ref> Poneman offered to fund a release by the band, so Thayil suggested he team up with Bruce Pavitt. Poneman offered to contribute $20,000 in funding for Sub Pop, effectively turning it into a full-fledged record label.<ref>[[Jim Berkenstadt|Berkenstadt, Jim]], and [[Charles R. Cross]]. ''Classic Rock Albums: Nevermind''. Schirmer, 1998. {{ISBN|0-02-864775-0}}, pg. 19</ref> Soundgarden signed to Sub Pop, and the label released "[[Hunted Down]]" in 1987 as the band's first single. The [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] of "Hunted Down", "Nothing to Say", appeared on the KCMU compilation tape ''Bands That Will Make Money'', which was distributed to record companies, many of whom showed interest in Soundgarden.<ref name="gilbert">Gilbert, Jeff. "Primecuts: Kim Thayil". ''Guitar School''. May 1994.</ref> Through Sub Pop, the band released the ''[[Screaming Life]]'' [[Extended play|EP]] in 1987, and the ''[[Fopp (EP)|Fopp]]'' EP in 1988, and a combination of the two, ''[[Screaming Life/Fopp]]'', in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|title=AllMusic ''Screaming Life/Fopp'' Review |url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r18514|pure_url=yes}}|website=[[AllMusic]]|author=Erlewine, Stephen Thomas|author-link=Stephen Thomas Erlewine|access-date=May 20, 2009}}</ref>

===''Ultramega OK'', major label signing, and ''Louder Than Love'' (1988–1990)===
Though major labels were courting the band, in 1988 they signed to the independent label [[SST Records]] for their debut album, ''[[Ultramega OK]]'', released on October 31, 1988. Cornell said the band "made a huge mistake with ''Ultramega OK''" because they used a producer suggested by SST who "didn't know what was happening in Seattle."<ref>"Yeah! I'm a Moody Bastard". ''[[Kerrang!]]''. August 19, 1995.</ref><ref>Alexander, Phil. "Soundgarden". ''[[Raw (music magazine)|Raw]]''. 1989.</ref> According to Steve Huey of [[AllMusic]], Soundgarden demonstrates a "[[The Stooges|Stooges]]/[[MC5]]-meets-[[Led Zeppelin|Zeppelin]]/[[Black Sabbath|Sabbath]] sound" on the album.<ref>{{cite web|last=Huey|first=Steve|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/ultramega-ok-mw0000202601|title=Ultramega OK|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130103100919/http://www.allmusic.com/album/ultramega-ok-mw0000202601 |date=c. 2009|archive-date=January 3, 2013 |work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=July 22, 2009}}</ref> [[Mark Miremont]] directed the band's first music video for "[[Flower (Soundgarden song)|Flower]]", which aired regularly on [[MTV]]'s ''[[120 Minutes]]''. Soundgarden promoted ''Ultramega OK'' on a tour in the United States in the spring of 1989, and a tour in Europe which began in May of that year—the band's first overseas tour.<ref>"Haughty Culture". ''[[Kerrang!]]''. April 8, 1989.</ref> ''Ultramega OK'' earned the band a [[Grammy Award]] nomination for [[Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance|Best Metal Performance]] in 1990.<ref name="latimes">{{cite news
 |url=http://theenvelope.latimes.com/factsheets/awardsdb/env-awards-db-search,0,7169155.htmlstory?searchtype=all&query=soundgarden 
 |title=Awards Database |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=August 2, 2008 |url-status=live
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713185338/http://theenvelope.latimes.com/factsheets/awardsdb/env-awards-db-search%2C0%2C7169155.htmlstory?searchtype=all&query=soundgarden |archive-date=July 13, 2011 }}</ref>

The band signed with [[A&M Records]] in mid-1988,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-rocket-soundgarden/166381666/|title=Soundarden|first=Johnny|last=Renton|work=The Rocket|page=7|date=August 1, 1988}}</ref> which had caused a rift between Soundgarden and its traditional audience. Thayil said, "In the beginning, our fans came from the punk rock crowd. They abandoned us when they thought we sold out the punk tenets, getting on a major label and touring with [[Guns N' Roses]]. There were fashion issues and social issues, and people thought we no longer belonged to their scene, to their particular sub-culture."<ref>Gilbert, Jeff. "Soundgarden". ''[[Guitar World]]''. December 1995.</ref> The band began work on its first album for a major label, but personnel difficulties caused a shift in the band's songwriting process.  According to Cornell, "At the time Hiro [Yamamoto] excommunicated himself from the band and there wasn't a free-flowing system as far as music went, so I ended up writing a lot of it."<ref name="colour">"Colour Me Badmotorfinger!". ''[[Raw (music magazine)|Raw]]''.
