===''Amo'' (2018–2019)===
{{Main|Amo (Bring Me the Horizon album)|l1=Amo}}
In August 2018, cryptic posters appeared in major cities throughout the world with the message "do you wanna start a cult with me?".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/bring-me-the-horizons-cult-posters-have-turned-up-in-chicago/|title=Bring Me the Horizon's "Cult" Posters Have Turned Up in Chicago|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=18 August 2018|access-date=17 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817225434/https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/bring-me-the-horizons-cult-posters-have-turned-up-in-chicago/|archive-date=17 August 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> The posters were attributed by major media outlets to the band only by their use of the hexagram logo previously used by the band. During this time the band themselves have not acknowledged their involvement with the campaign publicly. Each poster provided a unique phone number and a website address.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://joinmantra.org/|title=An Invitation To Salvation|website=Join Mantra|access-date=17 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817193349/http://joinmantra.org/|archive-date=17 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The website provided a brief message titled "An Invitation To Salvation" and shows the date of 21 August 2018. The phone lines placed fans on hold with lengthy, varied audio messages that changed frequently.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Alex|last=Darus|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-mantra-cult-us/|title=Bring Me the Horizon's Cryptic Album Teasing Has Reached the US|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=13 August 2018|access-date=17 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107080616/https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-mantra-cult-us/|archive-date=7 November 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Some of these messages reportedly end with a distorted audio clip of what was assumed to be new music from the band.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Stephen|last=Ackroyd|url=https://www.upsetmagazine.com/news/it-looks-like-bring-me-the-horizon-are-teasing-something-new|title=It looks like Bring Me The Horizon are teasing something new|magazine=Upset Magazine|date=11 August 2018|access-date=1 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817193325/https://www.upsetmagazine.com/news/it-looks-like-bring-me-the-horizon-are-teasing-something-new|archive-date=17 August 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Bring me the Horizon - 2019159205442 2019-06-08 Rock am Ring - 2106 - AK8I0006.jpg|thumb|right|Bring Me the Horizon at Rock am Ring in 2019]]
On 21 August, the band released the lead single "[[Mantra (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Mantra]]".<ref name="rock sound mantra">{{cite magazine|first=Brii|last=Jamieson|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-amo-mantra-tour|title=Bring Me The Horizon Have Announced The Details Of Their New Album, Announced A Tour|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=22 August 2018|access-date=28 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829003300/https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-amo-mantra-tour|archive-date=29 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Blabbermouth mantra">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-releases-music-video-for-mantra|title=Bring Me The Horizon Releases Music Video For 'Mantra'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=24 August 2018|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602013209/https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-releases-music-video-for-mantra|archive-date=2 June 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The following day the band announced their album ''[[Amo (Bring Me the Horizon album)|Amo]]'', released on 11 January 2019, along with a set of tour dates called the First Love World Tour.<ref name="rock sound mantra"/><ref name="Blabbermouth mantra"/>

On 21 October, the band released their second single "[[Wonderful Life (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Wonderful Life]]" featuring [[Dani Filth]], along with the tracklist for ''Amo''.<ref name="alternative press wonderful life">{{cite magazine|first=Rachel|last=Campbell|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-new-song-wonderful-life/|title=Bring Me The Horizon unleash "Wonderful Life", more album details|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=21 October 2018|access-date=22 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101042817/https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-new-song-wonderful-life/|archive-date=1 November 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Morton|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-release-new-song-wonderful-life-featuring-dani-filth|title=Bring Me The Horizon release new song Wonderful Life featuring Dani Filth|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=22 October 2018|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602013207/https://www.loudersound.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-release-new-song-wonderful-life-featuring-dani-filth|archive-date=2 June 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> That same day, the band announced that the album has been delayed and is now set for 25 January 2019.<ref name="alternative press wonderful life"/>

On 1 December, it was reported that during a show at London's Alexandra Palace a fan died in the [[mosh pit]] and was escorted by paramedics and security. A day later, it was confirmed by the band with a statement: "Words cannot express how horrified we are feeling this evening after hearing about the death of a young man at our show last night. Our hearts and deepest condolences go out to his family and loved ones at this terrible time. We will comment further in due course."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/report-fan-dies-in-the-pit-of-bring-me-the-horizon-show|title=Report fan dies in the pit of Bring Me The Horizon show|work=Metal Injection|date=1 December 2018|access-date=3 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181203095423/http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/report-fan-dies-in-the-pit-of-bring-me-the-horizon-show|archive-date=3 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-46441069|title=Bring Me The Horizon: Sister of fan who died at gig pays tribute|work=[[BBC]]|date=6 December 2018|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240214134739/https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-46441069|archive-date=14 February 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

===''Post Human: Survival Horror'', ''Nex Gen'' and Fish's departure (2020–present)===
{{Main|Post Human: Survival Horror|Post Human: Nex Gen}}
During the [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] lockdowns, the band shared that they were in a home studio, writing and recording material for their eighth record.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Skinner|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-to-live-stream-home-studio-footage-as-they-work-on-new-album-under-lockdown-2635030|title=Watch Bring Me The Horizon record their eighth album while under lockdown|work=[[NME]]|date=13 April 2020|access-date=21 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129035121/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-to-live-stream-home-studio-footage-as-they-work-on-new-album-under-lockdown-2635030|archive-date=29 January 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 June, the band released the single "[[Parasite Eve (song)|Parasite Eve]]" alongside an accompanying music video. On the same day, the band also announced a project that they have been working on titled ''Post Human'', which they said to be four EPs released throughout the next year which when combined would make an album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Trendell|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-post-human-new-album-oli-sykes-interview-2694847|title=Bring Me The Horizon tell us about their new 'survival horror song' 'Parasite Eve' and ambitious 'Post Human' project|work=[[NME]]|date=25 June 2020|access-date=25 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628070525/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-post-human-new-album-oli-sykes-interview-2694847|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Jackson|last=Langford|url=https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-me-the-horizon-are-planning-to-release-four-albums-over-the-next-year/|title=Bring Me The Horizon are planning to release four albums over the next year|work=[[Music Feeds]]|date=26 June 2020|access-date=26 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628103053/https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-me-the-horizon-are-planning-to-release-four-albums-over-the-next-year/|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The song was produced by [[Doom Eternal]] composer, [[Mick Gordon (composer)|Mick Gordon]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Rachael|last=Dowd|url=https://www.altpress.com/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-video/|title=See Bring Me The Horizon enter a horrifying new world in "Parasite Eve"|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=25 June 2020|access-date=21 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307184301/https://www.altpress.com/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-video/|archive-date=7 March 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 September, the band released with English singer [[Yungblud]] a collaborative single titled "[[Obey (Bring Me the Horizon and Yungblud song)|Obey]]" and its corresponding music video.<ref>{{cite web|first=Lauryn|last=Schaffner|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-yungblud-new-song-obey/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Drop New Song 'Obey' Featuring Yungblud|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=2 September 2020|access-date=2 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200903013704/https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-yungblud-new-song-obey/|archive-date=3 September 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 October, the band officially announced through social media that ''[[Post Human: Survival Horror]]'' would be released on 30 October 2020.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=James|last=Wilson-Taylor|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-post-human-survival-horror|title=Bring Me The Horizon Just Announced A New Release – 'Post Human: Survival Horror'|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=14 October 2020|access-date=14 October In December 2020, Fish said that the band had been writing "on and off" and would be focusing on their next release in early 2021. He also updated the group's release plan, saying that they "planned to do four EPs in a year, but [''Post Human: Survival Horror''] was almost an album, so I think the spacing will be a bit longer than intended, just because they're probably going to turn out bigger than intended."<ref>{{cite interview|first=Jordan|last=Fish|interviewer=Nick Ruskell|url=https://www.kerrang.com/features/bring-me-the-horizon-jordan-fish-my-year-2020/|title=Bring Me The Horizon's Jordan Fish: "My dream is to play live for three hours"|publisher=Wasted Talent|date=28 December 2020|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|access-date=31 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230212600/https://www.kerrang.com/features/bring-me-the-horizon-jordan-fish-my-year-2020/|archive-date=30 December 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Upon being released on physical formats on 22 January 2021, ''Post Human: Survival Horror'' would chart again and reach a new peak to gift Bring Me the Horizon their second UK number one on the [[UK Albums Chart]]. Two years after ''Amo'' would be the first to reach this feat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://store.hmv.com/store/music/cd/post-human-survival-horror|title=Post Human: Survival Horror – Bring Me the Horizon|publisher=[[HMV]]|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410145452/https://store.hmv.com/store/music/cd/post-human-survival-horror|archive-date=10 April 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Helen|last=Ainsley|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/bring-me-the-horizon-score-their-second-number-1-album-with-post-human-survival-horror-it-feels-like-a-really-exciting-time-for-us-__32332/|title=Bring Me The Horizon score their second Number 1 album with Post Human: Survival Horror: "It feels like a really exciting time for us"|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|date=29 January 2021|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205021559/https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/bring-me-the-horizon-score-their-second-number-1-album-with-post-human-survival-horror-it-feels-like-a-really-exciting-time-for-us-__32332/|archive-date=5 February 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> The band collaborated with singer [[Olivia O'Brien]] on a track titled "No More Friends". The song is from O'Brien's ''Episodes: Season 1' EP'' which was released on 11 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Reilly|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizons-oli-sykes-teams-up-with-olivia-obrien-on-new-track-no-more-friends-2967212|title=Bring Me The Horizon's Oli Sykes teams up with Olivia O'Brien on new track 'No More Friends'|work=[[NME]]|date=11 June 2021|access-date=12 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210612190612/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizons-oli-sykes-teams-up-with-olivia-obrien-on-new-track-no-more-friends-2967212|archive-date=12 June 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Artistry==

===Style and influences===

Among Bring Me the Horizon's earliest influences were bands like [[At the Gates]], [[Carcass (band)|Carcass]], [[Pantera]], [[Metallica]], [[Zao (American band)|Zao]], [[Arch Enemy]], [[The Dillinger Escape Plan]], [[Every Time I Die]], [[Norma Jean (band)|Norma Jean]], [[Skycamefalling]], [[Slipknot (band)|Slipknot]] and [[Poison the Well (band)|Poison the Well]];{{sfn|Patterson|2011|p=45}}<ref name="rockfreaks 1"/><ref name="Rocksound-olis mind"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-replaces-bury-your-dead-on-killswitch-engage-s-european-tour/|title=Bring Me The Horizon Replaces Bury Your Dead On Killswitch Engage's European Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=7 January 2007|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508213812/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-replaces-bury-your-dead-on-killswitch-engage-s-european-tour/|archive-date=8 May 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=MusicRadar>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicradar.com/news/drums/matt-nicholls-bring-me-the-horizon-interview-580345|title=Matt Nicholls (Bring Me The Horizon) interview|work=[[MusicRadar]]|date=31 July 2013|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910230523/http://www.musicradar.com/news/drums/matt-nicholls-bring-me-the-horizon-interview-580345|archive-date=10 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Kennelty|url=https://metalinjection.net/news/corey-taylor-recalls-discovering-bring-me-the-horizon-after-they-covered-eyeless|title=Corey Taylor Recalls Discovering Bring Me The Horizon After They Covered "Eyeless"|work=Metal Injection|date=30 October 2021|access-date=16 September 2025|quote=Obviously we all love Slipknot, we owe, like, you know, Bring Me the Horizon would not be here if Slipknot didn't exist, the first drum kit we ever got was the Corey Taylor kit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621201600/https://metalinjection.net/news/corey-taylor-recalls-discovering-bring-me-the-horizon-after-they-covered-eyeless|archive-date=21 June 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> and genres [[death metal]] like "[[Decapitated (band)|Decapitated]] or [[Suffocation (band)|Suffocation]]",<ref name="auto">{{cite web|first=Philip|last=Trapp|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-oli-sykes-names-band-that-first-got-him-into-metal/|title=Oli Sykes Names the Album That First Got Him Into Metal|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=February 22, 2022|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161055/https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-oli-sykes-names-band-that-first-got-him-into-metal/|archive-date=1 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> [[grindcore]], and [[emo]] have been cited by [[AllMusic]] writer Steward Mason.<ref name="allmusic bio">{{cite web|first=Stewart|last=Mason|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bring-me-the-horizon-p831398/biography|title=Bring Me the Horizon Allmusic|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=26 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110519130740/http://allmusic.com/artist/bring-me-the-horizon-p831398/biography|archive-date=19 May 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> However, as their sound developed, the band started to take influences from [[progressive rock]], [[post-rock]], [[dubstep]] and [[electronica]].{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=52}}<ref name="Rocksound-olis mind">{{cite magazine|first=Ben|last=Patashnik|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/features/article/inside-the-mind-of-oliver-sykes|title=Inside The Mind Of Oliver Sykes|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=28 September 2010|access-date=30 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120918115238/http://www.rocksound.tv/features/article/inside-the-mind-of-oliver-sykes|archive-date=18 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> According to Eli Enis of ''[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]'', the band "made chameleonic genre-hopping their artistic mission statement."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Eli|last=Enis|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/music/15-great-bands-sound-totally-different-their-debut-albums/|title=15 Great Bands That Sound Totally Different From Their Debut Albums|magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|date=21 March 2022|access-date=22 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415230537/https://www.revolvermag.com/music/15-great-bands-sound-totally-different-their-debut-albums/|archive-date=15 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> 

In an interview with ''[[NME]]'', Sykes said that ''[[That's the Spirit]]'' is a loose [[concept album]] about life's darker moods, such as depression, and a way of making light of it. He cited the [[alternative rock]] bands [[Jane's Addiction]], [[Panic! at the Disco]], [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]] and [[Radiohead]] as influences for the new album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gavin|last=Haynes|url=https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/bring-me-the-horizon-on-new-album-thats-the-spirit-and-riding-around-greek-islands-on-quad-bikes-16314|title=Bring Me The Horizon On New Album 'That's The Spirit' - And Riding Around Greek Islands On Quad Bikes|work=[[NME]]|date=21 July 2015|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240610030730/https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/bring-me-the-horizon-on-new-album-thats-the-spirit-and-riding-around-greek-islands-on-quad-bikes-16314|archive-date=10 June 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> They also cited [[Twenty One Pilots]] as an influence on the band's "next phase".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Maggie|last=Dickman|url=https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_twenty_one_pilots_influence_new_music/|title=Bring Me The Horizon talk new music, cite Twenty One Pilots as influence|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=8 March 2018|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161055/https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_twenty_one_pilots_influence_new_music/|archive-date=1 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

Oliver Sykes also said that his vocal style on Sempiternal was influenced by [[Chester Bennington]] and cited ''[[Hybrid Theory]]'' as one of his favorite albums.<ref>{{cite web|first=Merlin|last=Aldersladelast|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/oli-sykes-the-10-albums-that-changed-my-life|title=Bring Me The Horizon's Oli Sykes: 10 albums that changed my life|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=30 January 2019|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161055/https://www.loudersound.com/features/oli-sykes-the-10-albums-that-changed-my-life|archive-date=1 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> The album that got him to metal was [[Alive or Just Breathing]] by [[Killswitch Engage]].<ref name="auto"/> Jordan Fish said that the albums that influenced him most were [[Linkin Park]]'s ''Hybrid Theory'' and [[Deftones]]' ''[[White Pony]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/how-linkin-park-are-influencing-bring-me-the-horizons-new-music/|title=How Linkin Park Are Influencing Bring Me The Horizon's New Music|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=13 October 2020|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720180950/https://www.kerrang.com/how-linkin-park-are-influencing-bring-me-the-horizons-new-music/|archive-date=20 July 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

Bring Me the Horizon have attempted to grow and change with each album, believing they should be different.<ref name="RS-classic BFMV">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/bring-me-the-head-of-british-metal-revisited?|title=Rock Sound Classic Interviews: Matt Tuck vs Oli Sykes|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=21 March 2013|access-date=6 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812095853/http://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/bring-me-the-head-of-british-metal-revisited|archive-date=12 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Raziq Rauf, writing for ''[[Drowned in Sound]]'', described ''Count Your Blessings'' as possessing "Norma Jean-style thunderous riffs mixed with some dastardly [[Sludge metal|sludgy]] [[Doom metal|doom]] moments and more [[breakdowns (music)|breakdowns]] than your dad's old Nissan Sunny."<ref name="Dis-party music"/> ''[[Metal Hammer]]'' described ''Suicide Season'' as a "creative, critical and commercial success" for the band{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=52}} as they started to adopt a more eclectic style,<ref name="DIS-bio">{{cite web|url=http://drownedinsound.com/artists/Bring_Me_The_Horizon|title=Bring Me The Horizon // Drowned In Sound|work=[[Drowned In Sound]]|access-date=20 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919010404/http://drownedinsound.com/artists/Bring_Me_The_Horizon|archive-date=19 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> with its "crushingly heavy party deathcore".{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=50}} Leading up to its release, Oliver Sykes described it as "100% different to ''Count Your Blessings''" and noted the album sounds "more rock than metal".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.killyourstereo.com/news/1730/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-info/|title=Bring Me The Horizon new album info|work=Kill Your Stereo|date=27 August 2008|access-date=28 July 2012|quote="100% different" from "Count Your Blessings" [...] "More rock than metal. It's heavy though, and sounds a lot more fatter and beefier. We've also done some mellower tracks too."|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053437/http://www.killyourstereo.com/news/1730/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-info/|archive-date=21 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> As time went by, Bring Me the Horizon began rejecting their debut album ''Count Your Blessings'' and considered ''Suicide Season'' as their "Year Zero[...] ''[their]'' wipe-the-slate-clean time".{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=53}}

Bring Me the Horizon then moved even further away from deathcore with their third album ''[[There Is a Hell Believe Me I've Seen It. There Is a Heaven Let's Keep It a Secret.|There Is a Hell...]]'', which incorporated electronica, classical music and pop music into their metalcore style.<ref name="CANOE-horizons broadened">{{cite web|first=Darryl|last=Sterdan|url=http://jam.canoe.ca/Music/Artists/B/Bring_Me_The_Horizon/2010/11/18/16203866.html|title=Horizon broadens for young band|work=[[QMI Agency]]|publisher=[[Canoe Inc.]]|date=18 November 2010|access-date=20 March 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209031552/http://jam.canoe.ca/Music/Artists/B/Bring_Me_The_Horizon/2010/11/18/16203866.html|archive-date=9 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> This required more ambitious production feats, such as using a full [[choir]], a synthesised [[orchestra]] and glitched out vocals and breakdowns that were also toned down, favouring quiet atmospheric passages in song breaks.<ref name="Allmusic-TIAH Review">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/there-is-a-hell-believe-me-ive-seen-it-there-is-a-heaven-lets-keep-it-a-secret-r1951223/review|title=There Is a Hell, Believe Me I've Seen It, There is a Heaven, Let's Keep It a Secret – Bring Me the Horizon|work=[[Allmusic]]|access-date=14 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101016090736/http://www.allmusic.com/album/there-is-a-hell-believe-me-ive-seen-it-there-is-a-heaven-lets-keep-it-a-secret-r1951223/review|archive-date=16 October 2010|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="UG-Lee Guitar interview">{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Matera|url=http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/interviews/interviews/bring_me_the_horizon_interview_with_the_guitarist_lee_malia.html|title=Bring Me The Horizon: Interview With The Guitarist Lee Malia|work=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|date=11 February 2011|access-date=11 May 2012|quote=Yet, the album still includes the trademark elements that have become staples of the group's sound since 2006 – precision guitar riffs, venomously dark lyrics, massive breakdowns and gang vocals destined to be chants at the band's incendiary live shows. [...] We always thought 'why should we stick to the two guitars, drums and bass format? Why can't we have some production stuff brought into it and look at each song as a bigger picture?|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309190818/http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/interviews/interviews/bring_me_the_horizon_interview_with_the_guitarist_lee_malia.html|archive-date=9 March 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> For the writing of ''[[Sempiternal (album)|Sempiternal]]'', the band pooled far broader influences such as post-rock acts like [[This Will Destroy You]] and [[Explosions in the Sky]]<ref name="NME 3">{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Goodwyn|url=https://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/61173|title=Bring Me the Horizon Planning 'Post-Rock' Influenced Fourth Album|work=[[NME]]|date=29 December 2011|access-date=3 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120103090538/http://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/61173|archive-date=3 January 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> and from pop music.<ref name="AD-Sempiternal/Movies">{{cite web|first=Rick|last=Florino|url=http://www.artistdirect.com/entertainment-news/article/oli-sykes-of-bring-me-the-horizon-talks-sempiternal-movies-and-more/10565341|title=Oli Sykes of Bring Me The Horizon Talks "Sempiternal", Movies, and More|work=[[Artistdirect]]|date=20 May 2013|access-date=21 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609072721/http://www.artistdirect.com/entertainment-news/article/oli-sykes-of-bring-me-the-horizon-talks-sempiternal-movies-and-more/10565341|archive-date=9 June 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

to be labelled a pop metal act.<ref name="Metalinsider">{{cite web|first=Bram|last=Teitelman|url=http://www.metalinsider.net/new-music/bring-me-the-horizon-have-some-true-friends|title=Bring me the ===Songwriting and recording process===
In all the band's album notes, all of Bring Me the Horizon's lyrics are said to be written by lead vocalist [[Oli Sykes]] while all five members—as a band—were credited with writing the music. With the exception of ''Count Your Blessings'', the band has always written in a secluded location to avoid being distracted.<ref name="UG-Lee Guitar interview"/> Sykes' lyrics have a strong feeling of [[catharsis]] for him. He mainly draws from personal experience and has described the band's live performances as [[therapeutic]].<ref name="CANOE-horizons broadened"/> In 2006, when asked about the lyrics of ''Count Your Blessings'', as they had been criticised for their content solely fixated on [[broken heart|heartbreak]] and other themes that were called "shallow and meaningless", he responded "My life's never been that bad so I've not got that much to talk about."<ref name="Dis-party music"/>
Band members have described how the debut album was written in inner-city areas of [[Birmingham]] while being pressured to write and record songs to the deadlines given.<ref name="rockfreaks 1"/> This resulted in the band being unimpressed with the final product. However, for the writing process of ''Suicide Season'', the band realised that they preferred picking areas with less human contact to focus on the music; they wrote their second album in the Swedish countryside.<ref name="CANOE-expands horizons" /> During the writing of ''Suicide Season'', former and founding rhythm guitarist Curtis Ward wrote only two riffs of his rhythm parts of the album, mostly relying on Lee Malia to write all of the guitar sections of the album.<ref name="rockfreaks 1"/>

Malia has stated that the typical writing process involves Sykes writing the main structure of the songs, followed by Malia writing the main riff. From this, they would collaborate with each other to structure their work better and then later include the rest of the band in writing the rest of the song.<ref name="UG-Lee Guitar interview"/> The writing dynamic of ''Sempiternal'', typically featured Sykes, Malia, and newly introduced member Jordan Fish. According to Sykes, "Writing 'Sempiternal' was a completely different process...we worked from a computer, laying down ideas and riffs...bringing Jordan into the mix changed things completely; he opened up so many more possibilities."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-complete-sempiternal-details-revealed|title=Bring Me The Horizon: Complete 'Sempiternal' Details Revealed|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=14 January 2013|access-date=12 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128110846/https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-complete-sempiternal-details-revealed|archive-date=28 November 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> As they all took a break before writing their fourth album, they felt less of a need for an isolated writing environment.<ref name="Guardian-2013 interview">{{cite news|first=Ed|last=Cooper|url=http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2013/02/22/bring-me-the-horizon-this-album-needs-to-be-the-one-that-lasts-forever/|title=Bring Me The Horizon: This album needs to be the one that lasts forever|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|date=22 February 2013|access-date=26 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151023041236/http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2013/02/22/bring-me-the-horizon-this-album-needs-to-be-the-one-that-lasts-forever/|archive-date=23 October 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Image and legacy===
[[File:2014-06-05 Vainsteam Bring me the Horizon Oli Sykes 14.jpg|thumb|right|Sykes (pictured in 2014) has often been seen as the "poster boy" of Bring Me the Horizon's image.<ref name="Dis-party music"/>|233x233px]]

In their early years, the band was praised for their business acumen for selling mail-order merchandise and not relying on sales at live shows.<ref name="Kerrang 1501">{{cite journal|date=25 January 2014|title=The Untold Story Of Kerrang!: Bring Me The Horizon|journal=[[Kerrang!]]|issue= 1501|publisher= [[Bauer Consumer Media]] |editor= James McMahon |location= London, United Kingdom |issn=0262-6624}}</ref> Bring Me the Horizon's image has been characterised by the dominating personality of singer and front-man Oliver Sykes, and he has often been seen as the band's "Poster boy",<ref name="Dis-party music"/><ref name="Absolute Punk-TIAH Review">{{cite web|first=Drew|last=Beringer|url=http://www.absolutepunk.net/showthread.php?t=1939132|title=Bring Me the Horizon There Is a Hell, Believe Me I've Seen It. There Is a Heaven, Let's Keep it a Secret Review|work=[[AbsolutePunk]]|date=1 October 2010|access-date=10 October 2010|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121220093300/http://www.absolutepunk.net/showthread.php?t=1939132|archive-date=20 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> bearing the brunt of the band's controversial reputation.{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=50}} Early on, Bring Me the Horizon's image was infamously characterised by its members fashion sense and use of skinny-fit jeans, T-shirts with death metal band logos on the front and coloured hair/straightened hair. The band's image fit into what was called [[scene (subculture)|scene fashion]].{{sfn|Ritchie|2012|p=54}}<ref name="Kerrang 1501"/> The effect of their fashion aesthetics showed people, in show promoter Iain Scott's perspective, that "you don't have to look like a diabolical metalhead to be into metal or play in a metal band".{{sfn|Ritchie|2012|p=54}} However, their fashion conscious appearance earned them a "style over substance" label.{{sfn|Patterson|2011|p=45}}

Many controversies that occurred in their early years greatly affected public perceptions of the band, particularly an incident in 2007 at [[Nottingham]]'s [[Rock City (club)|Rock City]] venue, when a female fan claimed that Oliver Sykes had urinated on her.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-vocalist-accused-of-urinating-on-fan|title=Bring Me the Horizon Vocalist Accused Of Urinating On Fan|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=15 April 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024180625/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-vocalist-accused-of-urinating-on-fan/|archive-date=24 October 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> The charges were dropped due to a lack of evidence from CCTV footage in the area.{{sfn|Patterson|2011|p=47}} There were several documented examples of violence against the band during their live shows, including Sykes being [[pepper spray]]ed on stage;<ref name="RS-classic BFMV"/> and people getting onstage to assault the band.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Scott|last=Heisel|url=http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/bring_me_the_horizon_trade_blows_with_audience_members_in_salt_lake_city|title=Bring Me The Horizon trade blows with audience members in Salt Lake City|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=4 October 2011|access-date=5 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111209131017/http://www.altpress.com/news/entry/bring_me_the_horizon_trade_blows_with_audience_members_in_salt_lake_city|archive-date=9 December 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Despite the controversy over their image, various journalists have credited the band as being one of the most forward-thinking heavy bands in the UK.{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=52}} In 2012, just four years after the release of ''Suicide Season'', the album was inducted into [[Rock Sound]]'s ''Hall of Fame'', credited as a significant influence on the works of [[Asking Alexandria]], The Ghost Inside and [[While She Sleeps]]. It was credited as an influence on metalcore contemporaries Architects on ''[[Hollow Crown]]'' with their incorporation of keyboards and programming, and The Devil Wears Prada's ''[[Dead Throne]]'' for its more experimental and opinion-dividing sound.{{sfn|Ritchie|2012|p=56}} In an interview with ''Kerrang!'', guitarist Lee Malia remarked that the band wanted to go a bit more experimental, saying: "I always think we have been a year ahead of bands who are kind of just seeing what's cool and then copying it."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.kerrang.com/lee-malia-says-bmth-have-always-been-a-year-ahead-of-bands-who-just-copy-whats-cool|title=Lee Malia Says BMTH Have Always Been A Year Ahead Of Bands Who Just Copy What's Cool|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=22 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709175400/https://www.kerrang.com/lee-malia-says-bmth-have-always-been-a-year-ahead-of-bands-who-just-copy-whats-cool|archive-date=9 July 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

The band caused further controversy in February 2016 when Oliver Sykes trashed [[Coldplay]]'s table at the 2016 [[NME Awards]] during a live performance of Bring Me the Horizon's track "Happy Song".<ref name=":0">{{cite magazine|first=Ryan|last=Reed|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/bring-me-the-horizon-destroying-coldplays-nme-table-wasnt-protest-20160219|title=Bring Me the Horizon: Destroying Coldplay's NME Table Wasn't 'Protest'|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=19 February 2016|access-date=20 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220091036/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/bring-me-the-horizon-destroying-coldplays-nme-table-wasnt-protest-20160219|archive-date=20 February 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Sykes later stated that the act was not an act of "dirty protest", and suggested that it was "pure coincidence" that Coldplay were sitting at the table he trampled.<ref name=":0" /> Coldplay frontman [[Chris Martin]] admitted that he had never even heard of Bring Me the Horizon before the incident and he laughed it off, stating that "it was great, very 'rock and roll'".<ref>{{cite web|first=Elijah|last=Watson|url=http://uproxx.com/music/coldplay-bring-me-the-horizon-nme-awards-trashing-table/|title=Watch This Metal Band Trash Coldplay's Table At The 2016 NME Awards|work=UPROXX|date=18 February 2016|access-date=20 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219101937/http://uproxx.com/music/coldplay-bring-me-the-horizon-nme-awards-trashing-table/|archive-date=19 February 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

Another controversy occurred on April 20, 2024, when they posted a promotional ad for the Brisbane show in Australia which read, "If Jesus Christ returns, well just kill that fucker 2X," and caused some backlash among fans.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-slam-band-jesus-comments-concert-promo/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Fans Slam Band Over 'Jesus' Comments In Concert Promo|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=22 April 2024|access-date=14 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240510025206/https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-slam-band-jesus-comments-concert-promo/|archive-date=10 May 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Readers polls'''
* In a 2009 ''Rock Sound'' readers' poll, Bring Me the Horizon achieved both Best British Band and Worst British Band.<ref name="rock2009 poll">{{cite magazine|author=Dan|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/rock-sound-readers-poll-2009-the-results|title=Rock Sound Readers' Poll 2009: The Results|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=13 January 2010|access-date=4 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110907063833/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/rock-sound-readers-poll-2009-the-results|archive-date=7 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In 2011 ''[[The Guardian]]'' ran a poll for "Who should win the [[Mercury prize]]?" and used 50 albums, Bring Me the Horizon's third album ''There Is a Hell...'' won with 37%.<ref>{{cite web|author=Caspar Llewellyn Smith|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/musicblog/poll/2011/jul/12/mercury-prize-2011|title=Who should win the Mercury prize?|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=12 July 2011|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810174629/http://www.theguardian.com/music/musicblog/poll/2011/jul/12/mercury-prize-2011|archive-date=10 August 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In a 2013 [[Sirius XM]] published poll, Bring Me the Horizon won Best Song Discovery for "[[Go to Hell, for Heaven's Sake]]" with the [[Octane (Sirius XM)|Octane]] radio station.<ref>{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Chiocchio|url=http://blog.siriusxm.com/2013/12/03/best-of-2013-listener-poll/|title=Best of 2013 Listener Poll|work=[[Sirius XM]]|date=3 December 2013|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140923072553/http://blog.siriusxm.com/2013/12/03/best-of-2013-listener-poll/| archive-date=23 September 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In a 2013 Alternative Press readers poll, Bring Me the Horizon was nominated for four categories: Best Vocalist (Oliver Sykes; position 3),<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Cassie|last=Whitt|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_vocalist_of_the_year|title=2013 Readers Poll: Vocalist Of The Year|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=27 December 2013|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230121006/http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_vocalist_of_the_year|archive-date=30 December 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Best Keyboardist (Jordan Fish; position 1),<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Cassie|last=Whitt|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_keyboardist_of_the_year|title=2013 Readers Poll: Keyboardist Of The Year|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=27 December 2013|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131229075644/http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_keyboardist_of_the_year|archive-date=29 December 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> Single Of The Year ("[[Shadow Moses (song)|Shadow Moses]]"; position 2)<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Cassie|last=Whitt|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_single_of_the_year|title=2013 Readers Poll: Single Of The Year|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=26 December 2013|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230120941/http://altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_single_of_the_year|archive-date=30 December 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> and "Best Album Art" (Sempiternal; position 2).<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Cassie|last=Whitt|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_best_album_art|title=2013 Readers Poll: Best Album Art|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=26 December 2013|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231091104/http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/2013_readers_poll_best_album_art|archive-date=31 December 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>
* In 2021, ''Kerrang!'' readers voted "[[Die4U]]" as the best song and music video of the year. Bring Me the Horizon was also voted as the best band and best live band of the year. They were also voted as the second-best cover story of the year by ''Kerrang Magazine''.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-2021-readers-poll-results-what-music-has-ruled-your-year|title=The 2021 Readers' Polls Results: What has ruled your year?|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=21 December 2021|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240515012341/https://www.kerrang.com/the-2021-readers-poll-results-what-music-has-ruled-your-year|archive-date=15 May 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Velvet Revolver''' was an American [[hard rock]] [[Supergroup (music)|supergroup]] consisting of [[Guns N' Roses]] members [[Slash (musician)|Slash]] (lead guitar), [[Duff McKagan]] (bass, backing vocals) and [[Matt Sorum]] (drums, backing vocals), alongside [[Dave Kushner]] (rhythm guitar) formerly of [[Hardcore punk|punk]] band [[Wasted Youth (American band)|Wasted Youth]], and [[Scott Weiland]] (lead vocalist) formerly of [[Stone Temple Pilots]].  The band formed in 2002 and was active until 2008, when Weiland was fired from the band and subsequently rejoined Stone Temple Pilots.

In 2004, the band achieved commercial success with their debut album, ''[[Contraband (Velvet Revolver album)|Contraband]]''. Despite positive reviews, some critics initially described Velvet Revolver as a mere combination of Stone Temple Pilots and Guns N' Roses, and criticized them for a "disconnection" between Weiland and the rest of the band. With their single "[[Slither (song)|Slither]]", they won the 2005 [[Grammy Award]] for [[Grammy Award for Best Hard Rock Performance|Best Hard Rock Performance]]. The band released ''[[Libertad (Velvet Revolver album)|Libertad]]'' in 2007, driven by the release of the single "[[She Builds Quick Machines]]", and embarked on a tour with [[Alice in Chains]].

In April 2008, Weiland was fired from Velvet Revolver and [[2008 Stone Temple Pilots Reunion Tour|reunited with Stone Temple Pilots]]. Velvet Revolver was put on indefinite hiatus and in November of that year, requested to be released by their record label [[RCA Records]] to allow themselves "complete freedom to go through whatever process it would take to accomplish" replacing Weiland.

Although Velvet Revolver worked on new material and auditioned new singers following Scott Weiland's departure, the band has not released any new material and only performed publicly once since 2008, when they reunited with Weiland for a one-off reunion show on January 12, 2012, at a benefit concert. This proved to be their last performance together before Weiland's death on December 3, 2015. Slash and McKagan rejoined Guns N' Roses in 2016.

==History==

===Foundations (2001–2002)===
Slash, Duff McKagan, and Matt Sorum were members of the hard rock band [[Guns N' Roses]]. However, disagreements with singer [[Axl Rose]] resulted in Slash leaving the band in 1996 and McKagan departing in 1997 shortly before Sorum was fired.<ref name="Guns N' Roses AMG">{{cite web | author = Thomas Erlewine, Stephen |author2=Prato, Greg | title = Guns N' Roses Biography | publisher = [[AllMusic]] | access-date = November 14, 2010 | url = {{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p4416/biography|pure_url=yes}} | author-link = Stephen Thomas Erlewine}}</ref> Following their departures the trio focused on separate projects, with Slash reforming [[Slash's Snakepit]]<ref name="Slash AMG">{{cite web | last = Huey | first = Steve | title = Slash Biography | publisher = AllMusic | access-date = November 14, 2010 | url = {{AllMusic|class=artist|id=slash-p125919/biography|pure_url=yes}}}}</ref> and McKagan reforming [[10 Minute Warning]]<ref name="Duff McKagan AMG">{{cite web | last = Torreano | first = Bradley | title = Duff McKagan Biography | publisher = AllMusic| access-date = November 14, 2010 | url = {{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p104254/biography|pure_url=yes}}}}</ref><ref name="10 Minute Warning AMG">{{cite web | last = Ankeny | first = Jason | title = 10 Minute Warning Biography | publisher = AllMusic| access-date = November 14, 2010 | url = {{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p294177/biography|pure_url=yes}}}}</ref> as well as recording his second solo album,<ref name="Duff McKagan AMG"/> while Sorum rejoined [[the Cult]].<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | author-link2 = Anthony Bozza | title = [[Slash (autobiography)|Slash]] | publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/397 397] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref>

By 2001, Slash's Snakepit had disbanded for the second time.<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/410 410] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> Slash began working with [[the Black Crowes]] drummer [[Steve Gorman]] and an unnamed bassist on a new project:<ref name="VR Ultimate Guitar">{{cite web | last = Rosen | first = Steven | title = Velvet Revolver: 'We're Straight Up F--kin? Rock'. Part 2 | publisher = [[Ultimate Guitar Archive]] | date = February 11, 2006 | url = http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/interviews/interviews/velvet_revolver_were_straight_up_f--kin_rock_part_2.html}}</ref> writing the music for what would become "Fall to Pieces".<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/415 415] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> McKagan reformed [[Loaded (band)|Loaded]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Duff McKagan releases "Dark Days" as LOADED | publisher = [[Blabbermouth.net]] | date = June 20, 2001 | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=150 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20021120175914/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=150 | archive-date = November 20, 2002  | via= roadrunnerrecords.com| accessdate= }}</ref> previously his band for the tour in support of ''Beautiful Disease'',<ref name="Hard Force Magazine">{{cite web | last = Oliveira | first = Daniel | title = Duff McKagan Interview | work = Hard Force Magazine |date = June 1999| url = http://www.heretodaygonetohell.com/articles/showarticle.php?articleid=26}}</ref> with [[Geoff Reading]]. McKagan also added both [[Mike Squires (musician)|Mike Squires]] and [[Jeff Rouse (musician)|Jeff Rouse]] to the lineup.<ref name="Sputnikmusic Interview">{{cite web | last = de Sylvia | first = Dave | title = Duff McKagan's Loaded Interview | publisher = | website= Sputnikmusic.com | date = September 29, 2008 | url = http://www.sputnikmusic.com/feature.php?id=5403 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://archive.today/20121211052701/http://www.sputnikmusic.com/feature.php?id=5403 | archive-date = December 11, 2012 }}</ref> Following a tour of Japan in 2002,<ref>{{cite web | title = Former GUNS N' ROSES Bassist Announces West Coast, Japanese Dates | publisher = | website= Blabbermouth.net | date = January 12, 2002 | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=748 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110606051134/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=748 | archive-date = June 6, 2011 | via= roadrunnerrecords.com| accessdate= }}</ref> former [[Zilch (band)|Zilch]], [[Wasted Youth (American band)|Wasted Youth]], [[Electric Love Hogs]], and [[Dave Navarro]] guitarist [[Dave Kushner]] joined Loaded in place of Mike Squires.<ref name="Dave Kushner KNAC">{{cite web | last = Stingley | first = Mick | title = Exclusive! Interview With Velvet Revolver Guitarist Dave Kushner | publisher = | website= [[KNAC]].com | date = July 14, 2004 | url = http://www.knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=3136}}</ref>

===Formation (2002–2003)===
When musician [[Randy Castillo]] died from cancer in 2002, Slash, McKagan, and Sorum performed at a benefit concert to raise money and commemorate Castillo,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fcukingcontagious.net/WorDs/memorialconcert.html|title= Randy Castillo Benefit Concert - Exclusive| website= Fcukingcontagious.net|access-date= August 27, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007| page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/423 423] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> with [[Josh Todd (musician)|Josh Todd]] and Keith Nelson of [[Buckcherry]] as well as [[B-Real]] and [[Sen Dog]] of [[Cypress Hill]].<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/424 424] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> Recognizing that their musical relationship was still intact,<ref name="AMG Bio">{{cite web | last = Loftus | first = Johnny | title = Velvet Revolver Biography | publisher = AllMusic| access-date = July 20, 2010 | url = {{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p651389/biography|pure_url=yes}}}}</ref> the trio began rehearsing with Todd<ref name="AMG Bio"/> and Nelson, working on material that would become "Dirty Little Thing",<ref name="Contraband booklet">{{cite AV media notes | title = Contraband | title-link = Contraband (Velvet Revolver album) | others = Velvet Revolver | year= 2004 | publisher = [[RCA Records]] | type = CD booklet}}</ref> but eventually decided against forming a group with them.<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/425 425] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref><ref name="Slash p.426">{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/426 426] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> During a Loaded show at [[West Hollywood]]'s [[Viper Room]],<ref name="Slash p.426"/> McKagan re-introduced Dave Kushner to Slash, who had been friends in junior high and high school.<ref name="Dave Kushner KNAC"/><ref name="Slash p.427">{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash| publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/427 427] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> Kushner was invited to jam with the group and was soon invited to join with Slash, stating that "Dave brought a cool vibe to what [they] were doing. There was no deliberation; that was it, it was a perfect fit."<ref name="Slash p.427"/> Their former Guns N' Roses bandmate [[Izzy Stradlin]] also joined them for two weeks,<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | author-link2 = Anthony Bozza | title= Slash | publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/428 428] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> eventually suggesting that "Duff and [Stradlin] will sing and [they] will just do a club tour in a van." Slash states in his autobiography that it was hard to tell if Stradlin was serious or kidding.<ref name="Slash p.429">{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash | publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/429 429] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1 }}</ref> After auditioning Kelly Shaefer of [[Atheist (band)|Atheist]] and [[Neurotica (band)|Neurotica]],<ref name="AMG Bio"/> Stradlin left the group.<ref name="Slash p.429"/>

[[File:SaulHudson.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Guitarist [[Slash (musician)|Slash]] performing at a concert in [[Nijmegen]]]]
While Shaefer's audition was unsuccessful, the quartet continued auditioning for a lead singer. [[VH1]] filmed the recruitment process,<ref>{{Cite book | author = Slash | author2 = Bozza, Anthony | title = Slash | publisher = HarperCollins | year = 2007 | page = [https://archive.org/details/slashautobiograp0000unse/page/431 431] | isbn = 978-0-00-725775-1}}</ref> which was referred to as the temporary name "The Project".<ref name="AMG Bio"/> The resulting documentary was aired as ''VH1 Inside Out: The Rise of Velvet Revolver''. A number of lead singers auditioned for the band, including [[Stephen Shareaux]] of [[Kik Tracee]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://musiclegends.ca/stephen-shareaux-interview/|title=Stephen Shareaux Interview {{!}} KIK TRACEE frontman |date=June 22, 2017|work= Music Legends Online|access-date=May 21, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Steve Ludwin of [[Carrie (band)|Carrie]] and [[Little Hell (band)|Little Hell]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Supergroups like Chickenfoot never live up to the hype | publisher = | work= The Guardian| date = March 27, 2009 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/music/musicblog/2009/mar/27/supergroups-chickenfoot-velvet-revolver-ranconteurs}}</ref> [[Todd Kerns]], formerly of [[Age of Electric]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Canada's TODD KERNS Among Candidates For Singer Slot In Ex-GNR Project | publisher = | website= Blabbermouth.net| date = December 31, 2002 | url = The VELVET REVOLVER Boat | publisher = | website= Blabbermouth.net | date = September 8, 2004 | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=26629 | via= name= "Kerns/Albro" />  [[Travis Meeks]] of [[Days of the New]],<ref>{{cite web | title = DAYS OF THE NEW Frontman Collaborates With Former GUNS N' ROSES Members | publisher = | website= Blabbermouth.net | date = December 9, 2002 | url = http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=8101 | via= roadrunnerrecords.com| accessdate= }}</ref> and [[Ian Thornley]] of [[Big Wreck]].<ref>{{Cite web |first=Rocco | last= Sofee |date=2012-12-03 |title= Interview: Vocalist/Guitarist Ian Thornley Discusses Auditioning for Velvet Revolver and Reuniting with en}}</ref> [[Myles Kennedy]], formerly of the Mayfield Four, declined an invitation from Sorum to audition.<ref>{{cite web | title = SLASH, MYLES KENNEDY Interviewed In London | publisher = | website= Astbury]] of [[the Cult]] and [[Mike Patton]] of [[Faith No More]] also declined audition offers.<ref name="Classic Rock Contraband">{{Cite book | last = Milas | first = Alexander | title = Classic Rock presents Slash: Forbidden Fruit | year = 2010 | page = 123 | publisher = Future Pub. | isbn = 978-1-85870-318-3 }}</ref> The band were also interested in auditioning [[Stone Temple Pilots]] singer [[Scott Weiland]], who had become friends with McKagan after attending the same gym.<ref name= "Weiland Washington Post">{{cite news | last = Freedom du Lac | first = J | title = Velvet Revolver, A Legal Substance | newspaper = [[The Washington Post]] | date = August 2007 | url = http://blog.washingtonpost.com/virgin-festival/2007/08/post_1.html | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120913042749/http://blog.washingtonpost.com/virgin-festival/2007/08/post_1.html | archive-date = September 13, 2012 }}</ref><ref name="Weiland Details">{{cite web | last = Hendrickson | first = Matt | title = Scott Weiland Sobers Up . . . Again | work = [[Details (magazine)|Details]] | date = April 2010 | url = http://www.details.com/celebrities-entertainment/music-and-books/201004/scott-weiland-stone-temple-pilots-singer?currentPage=2 | access-date = December 10, 2010 | archive-date = August 14, 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120814004946/http://www.details.com/celebrities-entertainment/music-and-books/201004/scott-weiland-stone-temple-pilots-singer?currentPage=2 | url-status = dead }}</ref> Weiland once played on the same bill as Kushner,<ref name= "Slash p.432"/> and was in rehab at the same time as Sorum.<ref name="Slash p.432"/><ref name="Weiland Details"/> Weiland was sent two discs of material, and felt that the first disc "sounded like [[Bad Company]] gone wrong."<ref name="Weiland Washington Post"/> When he was sent the second disc, Weiland was more positive, comparing it to ''[[Core (Stone Temple Pilots album)|Core]]''-era Stone Temple Pilots,<ref name="Weiland Washington Post"/> though he turned them down because Stone Temple Pilots were still together.<ref name="Slash p.432"/>

{{Quote box
| width = 28%
| align = right
| quote = I just thought he was a great singer, and he'd always been on my mind for this band. He was the one vocalist that I knew had the kind of voice that would serve what we were going to do: he had a [[John Lennon]]-ish quality, a little bit of [[Jim Morrison]], and a touch of almost [[David Bowie]]. He was the best singer to come out in a long time in my opinion.<ref name="Slash p.432"/>
| source = —Slash on Scott Weiland
