In July 2018, Zombie embarked on the [[Twins of Evil: The Second Coming Tour]] in the US with co-headliner [[Marilyn Manson (band)|Marilyn Manson]] and special guest [[Deadly Apples]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/rob-zombie-marilyn-manson-kick-off-twins-of-evil-2-tour-detroit-8465106/|title=Rob Zombie and Marilyn Manson Unite For Beatles Cover as 'Twins Of Evil 2' Tour Kicks Off In Detroit|magazine=Billboard|access-date=December 29, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://montrealgazette.com/entertainment/local-arts/rockfest-founders-band-deadly-apples-touring-with-rob-zombie-marilyn-manson|title=Rockfest founder's band Deadly Apples touring with Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson|work=Montreal Gazette|last1=Kelly|first1=Brendan|date=May 16, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2019}}</ref> Zombie released a trailer to his third instalment of the ''Firefly'' trilogy in June 2019. The film—titled ''[[3 from Hell]]''—was released on [[DVD]] and [[Blu-ray]] on October 15, 2019, following a three-day theatrical release held by [[Fathom Events]] from September 16–18, 2019.

On August 1, 2017, Zombie announced on his Instagram page that he had begun working on his seventh studio album.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/rob-zombie-begins-work-on-new-album/ |title=Rob Zombie Begins Work On New Album |work=Blabbermouth.net |date=August 1, 2017 |access-date=August 19, 2017}}</ref> Guitarist [[John 5 (guitarist)|John 5]] described the album as "his ''[[Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band|Sgt. Pepper]]''", and called it "the best Zombie record that he's ever done."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://archive.blabbermouth.net/news/rob-zombies-next-album-is-definitely-his-sgt-peppers-lonely-hearts-club-band-says-john-5/|title=Rob Zombie Next Album Is 'Definitely' His 'Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band', Says JOHN 5|work=Blabbermouth.net|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=October 26, 2020|archive-date=October 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030034747/https://archive.blabbermouth.net/news/rob-zombies-next-album-is-definitely-his-sgt-peppers-lonely-hearts-club-band-says-john-5/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Zombie's first song in four years, "The Triumph of King Freak (A Crypt of Preservation and Superstition)", was released on October 30, 2020. Deemed a "ferocious blast of big guitar metal", it serves as the first single from his seventh album ''[[The Lunar Injection Kool Aid Eclipse Conspiracy]]'', released on March 12, 2021. The album was produced by [[Zeuss]], who also produced ''The Electric Warlock''. Zombie had focused primarily on filming in the years prior.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/rob-zombie-new-song-the-triumph-of-king-freak-1083458/|title=Rob Zombie Previews First Album in Five Years With 'The Triumph of King Freak|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Blistein|first=Jon|date=October 30, 2020|access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/rob-zombie-first-taste-of-new-album-to-arrive-a-week-from-today/|title=Rob Zombie: First Taste Of New Album To Arrive A Week From Today|work=Blabbermouth.net|date=October 23, 2020|access-date=October 26, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/rob-zombie-announces-the-lunar-injection-kool-aid-eclipse-conspiracy-album-first-single-king-freak-available-now/|title=Rob Zombie Announces 'The Lunar Injection Kool Aid Eclipse Conspiracy' Album; First Single 'King Freak' Available Now|work=Blabbermouth.net|date=October 30, 2020|access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref>

In May 2021, it was announced that Rob Zombie, [[John 5 (guitarist)|John 5]], [[Nikki Sixx]] and [[Tommy Clufetos]] formed a [[Supergroup (music)|supergroup]] called [[L.A. Rats]].<ref name="squires">{{cite web|last=Squires|first=John|title=Rob Zombie Forms New Band L.A. Rats With Nikki Sixx and First Song Will Debut Tomorrow!|url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/music/3666176/rob-zombie-forms-new-band-l-rats-nikki-sixx-first-song-will-debut-tomorrow/|work=[[Bloody Disgusting]]|date=May 20, 2021|access-date=May 20, 2021}}</ref> Their debut track, a cover of "[[I've Been Everywhere]]", is from the soundtrack to the [[Liam Neeson]] film ''[[The Ice Road]]''.<ref name="squires"/>

In June 2021, Zombie confirmed that he would direct a [[The Munsters (2022 film)|film adaptation]] of the television series ''[[The Munsters]]'', which was released on digital, DVD, Blu-Ray, and Netflix on September 27, 2022.

In May 2023, Zombie announced that he has begun working on his eighth solo album, which he hoped to have released by the summer of 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/rob-zombie-is-working-on-next-studio-album-its-going-good-he-says|title=ROB ZOMBIE Is Working On Next Studio Album: 'It's Going Good', He Says|publisher=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|access-date=May 26, 2023|date=May 25, 2023}}</ref>

In the fall of 2023, Zombie co-headlined the Freaks on Parade tour with [[Alice Cooper]], with [[Filter (band)|Filter]] and [[Ministry (band)|Ministry]] acting as the opening acts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://alicecooper.com/freaks-on-parade-tour|title=Freaks on Parade Tour|website=alicecooper.com|date=January 30, 2023 |access-date=September 25, 2023}}</ref> The tour spanned one month, lasting from August 24, 2023 until September 24, 2023, visiting 19 venues across the United States and Canada.

== Artistry ==
=== Musical style ===
[[File:20140615-132-Nova Rock 2014-Rob Zombie-Rob Zombie.JPG|thumb|270px|Zombie at [[Nova Rock Festival|Nova Rock]] 2014]]
Zombie's music has been noted for its use of [[horror film|horror and suspense elements]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maximumink.com/index.php/articles/permalink/rob_zombie/ |title=Rob Zombie |website=Maximumink.com |date=November 1, 2009 |access-date=June 21, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ifc.com/fix/2012/08/heavy-metal-and-horror |title=Heavy Metal and Horror |website=IFC |date=August 14, 2012 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> which is inspired by Zombie's love of horror films.<ref>{{cite web|last=Vo |first=Alex |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/comic_con_2009/news/1834259/five_favorite_films_with_rob_zombie/ |title=Five Favorite Films With Rob Zombie |website=Rotten Tomatoes |date=July 26, 2009 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> Zombie's music also contains elements commonly found in [[heavy metal music]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://delafont.com/music_acts/rob-zombie.htm |title=Rob Zombie booking|website=Delafont.com |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.comingsoon.net/news/movienews.php?id=54316 |title=Exclusive: Rob Zombie Approached for Heavy Metal |website=ComingSoon.net |date=April 8, 2009 |access-date=November 25, 2012 |archive-date=April 11, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090411102714/http://www.comingsoon.net/news/movienews.php?id=54316 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gantdaily.com/2012/06/21/heavy-metal-musician-rob-zombie-to-produce-flyers-flick/ |title=Heavy metal musician Rob Zombie to produce Flyers flick |website=GantDaily.com |date=June 21, 2012 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> Zombie's music has been described as "melding metal with industrial, hypnotic rhythms and haunting sounds" and having a "complicated beat, distinctive vocals and a killer story line".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roughedge.com/cdreviews/z/robzombie.htm |title=Rob Zombie CD Reviews |publisher=Rough Edge |date=May 20, 2012 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> Zombie's songs have also been known to feature quotes and samples from classic horror films.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://celebritywonder.ugo.com/html/robzombie_trivia1.html |title=Rob Zombie News and Trivias |website=Celebritywonder.ugo.com |access-date=November 25, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110412122734/http://celebritywonder.ugo.com/html/robzombie_trivia1.html |archive-date=April 12, 2011  }}</ref> Numerous songs on his debut album, ''[[Hellbilly Deluxe]]'', feature quotes from classic horror films that Zombie grew up with.<ref name="reocities.com"/> Zombie has classified himself as a [[Heavy metal music|metal]] musician, and stated "It felt like hard rock and heavy metal had really been struggling you know, like top of the charts – it felt like they were being kicked to the curb for a long time. It was almost like you were doing something but you feel like nobody cares anymore so now you're just chuggin' along doing what you do and it's like the world had forgotten. However it's felt like in the last few years that's kind of changed and you feel it coming back."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/rob-zombie-interview-band-lineup-upcoming-album-touring-more/ |title=Rob Zombie on Band Chemistry, Upcoming Album, Touring + More |website=Loudwire.com |date=May 11, 2012 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref>

In their review of ''Venomous Rat Regeneration Vendor'' (2013), Music Enthusiast commented on Zombie's musical style "If you are a fan of Rob Zombie's, or even if you aren't, you can definitely recognize his style of music- that is to say, if Alice Cooper wrote songs for strip clubs. Rob Zombie albums have always had bombastic, almost danceable grooves, over the top guitar effects [...] and loads of B-movie sci-fi/horror lyrics."<ref name="musicenthusiast" /> He is also noted for using "spoken word lyrics" in numerous songs, a style he began while with White Zombie.<ref name="musicenthusiast" /> [[AllMusic]] compared the musical themes of ''Hellbilly Deluxe'' to a White Zombie record, stating it was "complete with thunderous industrial rhythms, drilling [[Heavy metal music|metal]] guitars, and [[B movie|B-movie]] obsessions."<ref name="Allmusic 4">{{cite web|url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r373740/review|pure_url=yes}}|title=Hellbilly Deluxe - Rob Zombie|website=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref> ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' spoke about the album's horror film qualities, stating it had "concocted a veritable blood feast of hair-raising guitars, spine-tingling drum loops, and a cast of ghoulish characters who could be refugees from an old William Castle horror flick."<ref name="ew.com">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/article/1998/09/18/hellbilly-deluxe/|magazine=Entertainment Weekly|title=Hellbilly Deluxe|first=Marc|last=Weingarten|date=September 18, 1998|access-date=June 21, 2020|archive-date=August 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803211056/https://ew.com/article/1998/09/18/hellbilly-deluxe/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Legends Magazine wrote that "the songs follow the same formula of anger, sex, death, monster, demon, zombie, satanic, drug abuse kinda raw drive a tractor over your neighbor's skull kinda hate the world so I'll burn it all down music."<ref name="legendsmagazine.net">{{cite journal|url=http://www.legendsmagazine.net/82/zombie.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010219151630/http://www.legendsmagazine.net/82/zombie.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=February 19, 2001|title=CD Review - Rob Zombie - "Hellbilly Deluxe" |journal=Legends Magazine |issue=82}}</ref> AllMusic wrote in their review of ''American Made Music to Strip By'' that ''Hellbilly Deluxe'' had a "sexy, sleazy, horror-movie vibe".<ref name="remix"/>

While ''The Sinister Urge'' continues the themes of horror and suspense, it is noted as featuring more dance-oriented beats in songs such as "[[Never Gonna Stop (The Red Red Kroovy)]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.recoilmag.com/gun-legends-5-sub-machine-gun-terbaik-sepanjang-masa/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061018104856/http://recoilmag.com/cd_reviews/rob_zombie_the_sinister_urge.html |url-status=dead |title=Gun Legends: 5 Sub Machine Gun Terbaik Sepanjang Masa|archive-date=October 18, 2006}}</ref> Zombie claimed that whereas ''Hellbilly Deluxe'' featured electronics, ''The Sinister Urge'' was recorded with a live band as to emphasize the instrumentals.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|title=Argentina vs. S. Korea, 2010 World Cup – Formations|url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/document/tournament/competition/01/24/79/59/20%5f0617%5farg-kor%5ftacticalstartlist.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100705003050/http://www.fifa.com/mm/document/tournament/competition/01/24/79/59/20_0617_arg-kor_tacticalstartlist.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 5, 2010|access-date=June 3, 2012}}</ref> With the ''Educated Horses'' album, Zombie further distanced himself from the sound of his first two albums. Zombie described the album as experimental, and explored a number of acoustic productions with [[John 5 (guitarist)|John 5]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.audiohead.net/interviews/robzombie/|title=Interview: Rob Zombie|publisher=Audiohead|first=Steph|last=Jorgl}}</ref> Despite a shift in sound, many of the album's lyrics feature horror elements found on his prior releases.<ref name="RollStone"/> ''Hellbilly Deluxe 2'', Zombie's fourth studio album, saw a return to the heavy metal sound of his early releases.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rob Zombie Signs With Loud & Proud/Roadrunner Records |work=Blabbermouth.net |publisher=Roadrunner Records |date=October 28, 2009 |url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/BLABBERMOUTH.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=129459 |access-date=October 28, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091031233046/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=129459 |archive-date=October 31, 2009  }}</ref> The album was considered a direct sequel to his debut studio album, with which it shares a name. ''Venomous Rat Regeneration Vendor'' continued these themes, and features "bass-heavy" beats.<ref name="musicenthusiast"/> The record was deemed a throwback to his debut album due to similar lyrical and sonic themes.<ref name="musicenthusiast" />

=== Influences ===
Both Zombie's music and film work draws influence from classic horror and suspense films, with Zombie citing the 1970s as the "last great time where films were being made for the sake of the film and not for the sake of the money."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/rob-zombie-1798208595|title=Rob Zombie|first=Scott|last=Tobias|website=[[The A.V. Club]]|date=August 2, 2005 }}</ref> Zombie has cited artists such as [[Alice Cooper]],<ref>{{cite web |date=2006-05-22 |url=http://www.vh1classic.com/view/playlist/1531879/87125/Heavy_The_Story_of_Metal_Heavy_Q_and_A/First_Metal_Moment_Q_and_A/index.jhtml |title="Metal: As Defined By Gods" from Heavy: The Story of Metal |website=Vh1classic.com |access-date=November 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100430162414/http://www.vh1classic.com/view/playlist/1531879/87125/Heavy_The_Story_of_Metal_Heavy_Q_and_A/First_Metal_Moment_Q_and_A/index.jhtml |archive-date=April 30, 2010  }}</ref> [[Kiss (band)|Kiss]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/peter-criss-performs-kiss-god-of-thunder-with-rob-zombie-at-93-3-wmmr-mmrbq-video/|title=Peter Criss Performs Kiss' 'God Of Thunder' With Rob Zombie At 93.3 WMMR MMR*B*Q (Video)|publisher=Blabber Mouth|date=May 11, 2014}}</ref> [[Queen (band)|Queen]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gibson.com/News-Lifestyle/News/en-us/Rob-Zombie-Loves-820.aspx|title=Rob Zombie Loves Elton John, Queen|publisher=Gibson|date=August 20, 2010}}</ref> and [[Elton John]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rttnews.com/1399414/elton-john-and-queen-popular-with-hard-rocker-rob-zombie.aspx|title=Elton John And Queen Popular With Hard Rocker Rob Zombie|publisher=RTT News|date=August 22, 2010}}</ref> as influences during his childhood.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spinner.com/2010/08/19/rob-zombie-queen-elton-john/ |title=Rob Zombie Influenced by Queen and Elton John?!? |publisher=Spinner |date=August 19, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2012 |archive-date=June 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624042818/http://www.spinner.com/2010/08/19/rob-zombie-queen-elton-john/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Zombie claimed that the first record he ever bought was an Alice Cooper album.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rzr.online.fr/docs/zombie/alicecooper.htm |title=Alice Cooper & Rob Zombie : Influences, Interviews (Zombie land 2) |website=Rzr.online.fr |date=October 28, 1995 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> [[Metallica]], [[Black Sabbath]], [[Judas Priest]], [[Slayer]], [[Ministry (band)|Ministry]], [[Pantera]], [[Sepultura]], [[Black Flag (band)|Black Flag]] and [[Twisted Sister]] were also cited as influences by Zombie.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/artists/rob-zombie/related-artists/?filter=influencedBy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130814194825/http://www.mtv.com/artists/rob-zombie/related-artists/?filter=influencedBy|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2013|title=Artist Influences for Rob Zombie - MTV|publisher=MTV}}</ref> Zombie claimed his mother would not allow him to watch horror films, namely ''[[The Texas Chain Saw Massacre]]'' (1974),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,615052,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090602131245/http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,615052,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 2, 2009 |title=Rob Zombie's TV Influence – Rob Zombie |work=People |date=May 21, 1999 |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> which later served as an influence on Zombie's films ''House of 1000 Corpses'' and ''The Devil's Rejects''.<ref>{{cite web|author=Tim Harden |url=http://www.texaschainsawmassacre.net/Homages/Homages.htm |title=Homages to the Texas Chain Saw Massacre |website=Texaschainsawmassacre.net |access-date=November 25, 2012}}</ref> Zombie has directed the majority of his music videos as a solo artist, with numerous releases being influenced or referencing horror films. The music video for his single "[[Living Dead Girl (song)|Living Dead Girl]]" is based upon the silent horror film ''[[The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari]]'' (1920),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hollywood-movies.yoexpert.com/hollywood-movies-general/what-is-film-s-influence-on-music-31995.html |title=What is film's influence on music? |website=Hollywood-movies.yoexpert.com |access-date=November 25, 2012 |archive-date=January 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130128040926/http://hollywood-movies.yoexpert.com/hollywood-movies-general/what-is-film-s-influence-on-music-31995.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> while his video for "Never Gonna Stop (The Red Red Kroovy)" was heavily inspired by ''[[A Clockwork Orange (film)|A Clockwork Orange]]'' (1971).<ref>{{cite web |author=Madison |url=http://unrealitymag.com/index.php/2010/06/11/music-videos-with-clockwork-orange-references/ |title=Seven Music Videos Influenced by A Clockwork Orange |website=Unrealitymag.com |date=June 11, 2010 |access-date=November 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017102057/http://unrealitymag.com/index.php/2010/06/11/music-videos-with-clockwork-orange-references/ |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His film ''The Lords of Salem'' was inspired by the horror classic ''[[The Shining (film)|The Shining]]'' (1980).<ref>{{YouTube|B2cv_UGnV98|Rob Zombie Goes Big With The Lords of Salem}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
[[File:Rob Zombie Comiccon.JPG|thumb|upright|Zombie in 2007]]
Zombie dated his [[White Zombie (band)|White Zombie]] bandmate [[Sean Yseult]] from 1984 until 1991, though they continued to work in the band together after their breakup.<ref name="girlsandcorpses.com" /> Zombie began dating actress [[Sheri Moon Zombie|Sheri Moon]] in 1993,<ref name="girlsandcorpses.com" /> and they were married at [[Graceland Wedding Chapel]] in [[Las Vegas]] on October 31, 2002.<ref>{{cite web|website=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2007-aug-19-ca-robzombie19-story.html|title=A marriage made in hell|first=Paul|last=Cullum|date=August 19, 2007|access-date=July 22, 2021}}</ref> They originally set their wedding date for November 9,<ref>{{cite web|url= https://nypost.com/2013/04/14/the-evil-dreads/ |title=The Evil Dreads |website=New York Post |date=April 14, 2013|first=Gary|last=Letlen|access-date=December 13, 2021}}</ref> but eloped 10 days before.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://watchingrobertpickton88015.yuku.com/topic/1979/FICTIONAL-MONSTERS-KILLERS-ETC?page=1#.UDAibaNpf6M |title=Fictional Monsters/Killers/Etc in "Watching/reading fictionalized crime stories." Forum |website=Watchingrobertpickton88015.yuku.com |date=December 10, 2008 |access-date=November 24, 2012}}</ref> They split their time between a home in [[Los Angeles]] and a farm in [[Connecticut]].<ref name=ny>{{cite web|work=[[New York Post]]|url=https://nypost.com/2019/09/11/3-from-hell-star-sheri-moon-zombie-dishes-on-making-gore-look-glam/|title='3 From Hell' star Sheri Moon Zombie dishes on making gore look glam|last=Hoffman|first=Barbara|date=September 11, 2019|archive-url=https://archive.today/20190916213738/https://nypost.com/2019/09/11/3-from-hell-star-sheri-moon-zombie-dishes-on-making-gore-look-glam/|archive-date=September 16, 2019}}</ref>

Zombie's public image has often been denoted by his long hair, large beard, [[Industrial music|industrial]] fashion sense, and horror-themed makeup.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://herocomplex.latimes.com/uncategorized/a-zombie-that-never-sleeps-rob-zombie-has-sickness-that-keeps-in-in-motion/ |title=A zombie that never sleeps: Rob Zombie has 'sickness' that keeps him in motion |website=Herocomplex.latimes.com |date=August 26, 2009 |access-date=March 14, 2016}}</ref> A self-described [[Veganism|ethical vegan]], he and his wife use their Connecticut property to house rescued farm animals.<ref>{{Cite web|date=November 14, 2019|title=Rob Zombie on Woodstock Warrior Award, Fighting for Animals, Why Veganism Is Punk|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/culture/rob-zombie-woodstock-warrior-award-fighting-animals-why-veganism-punk|access-date=November 9, 2020|website=Revolver|language=en}}</ref> He originally became a [[Vegetarianism|vegetarian]] in 1982 after viewing footage of a slaughterhouse. He is a supporter of [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals|PETA]] and was thanked by the organization for his realistic portrayal of the [[Cruelty to animals#Alleged link to human violence and psychological disorders|link between childhood animal abuse and psychopathy]] in his [[Halloween (2007 film)|remake of ''Halloween'']].<ref name="sammag">{{cite web |last=Bliss |first=Karen |url=http://www.samaritanmag.com/1392/rob-zombie-animals-always-need-be-protected |title=Rob Zombie: Animals Always Need To Be Protected |website=Samaritanmag.com |access-date=February 25, 2013 |archive-date=February 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160223083301/http://www.samaritanmag.com/1392/rob-zombie-animals-always-need-be-protected |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Zombie generally refrains from sharing his political and religious beliefs with the public, though he has mentioned that his mother once contemplated becoming a nun.<ref name="nun" /> In the same interview, he said that he [[Teetotalism|avoids all alcohol and drugs]] because he "certainly didn't achieve anything by being wasted and fucked up".<ref name="nun">{{cite web|url=http://www.dailykos.com/story/2008/11/13/660456/-|title=Rob Zombie: An Unorthodox Champion of American Values|website=Dailykos.com|date=November 13, 2008}}</ref> In a separate interview, he said that he does not believe in an [[afterlife]] and the concept of [[Heaven]] was "insane", believing that "this life is all you get".<ref name="afterlife" /> He also said that he does not believe in concepts such as [[unidentified flying objects|UFOs]], [[extraterrestrial life|aliens]], or [[Bigfoot]].<ref name="afterlife">{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9xuKhy13rA4| archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211027/9xuKhy13rA4| archive-date=2021-10-27|title=Rob Zombie Pt1 - What happens when you Die| date=April 15, 2008|publisher=[[YouTube]]|access-date=December 22, 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He criticized the initial cancellation of the 2020 horror film ''[[The Hunt (2020 film)|The Hunt]]'' following an outcry from U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] and [[Trumpism|his supporters]], stating, "As far as [canceling] ''The Hunt'', that's just a bullshit [[sacrificial lamb]] that solves nothing in society, but they always do that. If it wasn't that movie it would have been a video game or sometimes it was somebody's rock album."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Andrews|first=Travis M.|title=Trump weighed in on a movie, then the studio canceled it. Now the director has something to say.|language=en-US|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/arts-entertainment/2019/08/19/trump-weighed-movie-then-studio-canceled-it-now-director-has-something-say/|access-date=November 9, 2020|issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Nichols|first1=Mackenzie|date=September 12, 2019|title=Rob Zombie on 'The Hunt' Cancellation and Working With Low Budgets|url=https://variety.com/2019/film/news/rob-zombie-3-from-hell-the-hunt-1203319711/|access-date=November 9, 2020|website=Variety|language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Chevelle''' is an American [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Grayslake, Illinois]], in 1995. The band was originally composed of brothers [[Pete Loeffler]] (lead vocals and guitar) and Sam Loeffler (drums and percussion) with Matt Scott (bass and backing vocals). Scott was replaced with Sam and Pete's brother, Joe Loeffler, in 1996. When Joe left the band in 2005, Geno Lenardo filled in as touring bassist until he was replaced with Pete and Sam's brother-in-law, [[Dean Bernardini]]. Bernardini departed the band in 2019, and in 2021, Kemble Walters joined as a touring bassist.

The band's first studio album, ''[[Point No. 1|Point #1]]'', was released on small record label [[Squint Entertainment]]. Chevelle's second album, ''[[Wonder What's Next]]'' (2002), was certified double platinum by the [[RIAA]] after a debut at No.&nbsp;14 on the United States albums chart, [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. ''[[This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)]]'' (2004), the band's third album, debuted at No.&nbsp;8 and has been certified platinum. Chevelle has since released seven more albums: ''[[Vena Sera]]'' (2007), ''[[Sci-Fi Crimes]]'' (2009), ''[[Hats Off to the Bull]]'' (2011), ''[[La Gárgola]]'' (2014), ''[[The North Corridor]]'' (2016), ''[[NIRATIAS]]'' (2021), and ''[[Bright as Blasphemy]]'' (2025). Other releases from Chevelle include two live albums, two DVDs, and two compilation albums. As of 2022, the band has sold over 6 million records.

== History ==

=== Formation, ''Point #1'', and ''Wonder What's Next'' (1995–2003) ===
{{Main|Point No.&nbsp;1|Wonder What's Next|l1 = Point #1}}

[[File:Chevelle logo (band).svg|thumb|Logo used since Wonder What's Next.]]
Chevelle formed in 1995 in [[Grayslake, Illinois]], when brothers [[Pete Loeffler]] and Sam Loeffler started learning to play music.<ref name="AMG">{{Cite web|first=Tracy|last=Frey|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/chevelle-mn0000091549/biography|title=Chevelle Biography - AllMusic|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=February 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013149/https://www.allmusic.com/artist/chevelle-mn0000091549/biography|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="crossrhythms">{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Style|url=http://www.crossrhythms.co.uk/articles/music/Chevelle_The_Chicago_hard_rock_trio_breaking_big_in_the_mainstream/8257/p1/|title=Chevelle: The Chicago hard rock trio breaking big in the mainstream|work=Crossrhythms.co.uk|date=October 30, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122163025/https://www.crossrhythms.co.uk/articles/music/Chevelle_The_Chicago_hard_rock_trio_breaking_big_in_the_mainstream/8257/p1/|archive-date=November 22, 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> Pete started playing guitar and singing and Sam began playing drums in their parents' garage.<ref name="AMG"/> Bassist Matt Scott was in the band until 1996.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik">{{cite web|url=https://www.sputnikmusic.com/bands/Chevelle/228/|title=Chevelle reviews, music, news|work=[[Sputnikmusic]]|access-date=January 12, 2021}}</ref> Their youngest brother, Joe Loeffler, joined the band replacing Scott.<ref name="AMG"/><ref name="crossrhythms"/> Each member was a self-taught musician.<ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik" /> The name Chevelle came from the band members' passion for fast cars.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Mike|last=Sanders|url=http://loudwire.com/chevelle-frontman-pete-loeffler-hot-rods-hats-off-to-the-bull-more/|title=Chevelle Frontman Pete Loeffler Dishes on Hot Rods, 'Hats Off to the Bull' + More|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=April 26, 2012|access-date=March 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411055820/http://loudwire.com/chevelle-frontman-pete-loeffler-hot-rods-hats-off-to-the-bull-more/|archive-date=April 11, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> It was also a car their father liked, the [[Chevrolet Chevelle]].<ref name="Christian music">{{Cite web|url=http://christianmusic.com/chevelle/bio.html|title=Chevelle|work=Christian Music|access-date=December 28, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020804153524/http://christianmusic.com/chevelle/bio.html|archive-date=August 4, 2002|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band started playing small outdoor concerts and clubs around [[Chicago, Illinois|Chicago]], [[Illinois]].<ref name="AMG" />

Chevelle recorded a seven-track [[Demo (music)|demo]] known as ''The Blue Album'', released in 1998.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/> The band played small concerts for the next three years until they signed with [[Steve Taylor]]'s [[Squint Entertainment]],<ref name="AMG"/><ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/> a [[contemporary Christian music]] label. The band recorded with [[Steve Albini]] for 17 days in [[Electrical Audio]] studios and released its first full-length album, ''[[Point No.&nbsp;1|Point #1]]'' in 1999.<ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref>{{cite journal|last=Olson|first=Chad|date=July–August 1999|title=Album Reviews: Chevelle ''Point #1''|journal=[[HM (magazine)|HM]]|issue=78|issn=1066-6923}}</ref><ref name="JFH#1">{{cite web|first=John|last=DiBase|url=http://www.jesusfreakhideout.com/cdreviews/PointNo1.asp|title=Chevelle, "Point #1" Review|work=Jesus Freak Hideout|date=September 11, 1999|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011112235310/http://www.jesusfreakhideout.com/cdreviews/PointNo1.asp|archive-date=November 12, 2001|url-status=live}}</ref> Two singles were released from the album with accompanying music videos, "[[Point No. 1 (song)|Point #1]]" and "Mia".<ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Knopper|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1999-09-10-9909100222-story.html|title=Chevelle Built On Hard Rock And Brotherly Tolerance|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=September 9, 1999|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://archive.today/20220613033117/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1999-09-10-9909100222-story.html|archive-date=June 13, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The songs received [[GMA Dove Award]]s in 2000 and "Point #1" in 2001.<ref name="DOVE_HS">"{{cite web|url=http://www.doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?cid=32|title=Dove Award Recipients for Hard Music Recorded Song|work=[[Gospel Music Association]]|access-date=November 15, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020106001828/http://www.doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?cid=32|archive-date=January 6, 2002|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album won "Hard Music Album" in the 2000 Dove Awards.<ref name="DOVE_00">"{{Cite web|url=http://doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?year=2000|title=Dove Award Recipients for Hard Music Album|work=[[Gospel Music Association]]|access-date=November 15, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020406020434/http://doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?year=2000|archive-date=April 6, 2002|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album was well received by ''Phantom Tollbooth'' and ''[[HM (magazine)|HM Magazine]]'',<ref name="Tollbooth#1">{{cite web|first=James|last=Stewart|url=http://www.tollbooth.org/review99/chevelle.html|title=Point #1|work=The Phantom Tollbooth|date=July 28, 1999|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010224005058/http://www.tollbooth.org/review99/chevelle.html|archive-date=February 24, 2001|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="HM_78">{{Cite journal|first=Chad|last=Olson|url=http://www.hmmagazine.com/issue78/78AlbumReviews.htm|title=Album Reviews: Chevelle Point #1|journal=[[HM (magazine)|HM Magazine]]|date=July–August 1999|access-date=April 24, 2007|issue=78|issn=1066-6923|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010717025343/http://www.hmmagazine.com/issue78/78AlbumReviews.htm|archive-date=July 17, 2001|url-status=dead}}</ref> yet was criticized for its repetitive song structures by Jesus Freak Hideout, a Christian music website.<ref name="JFH#1"/> The band's label was going through legal troubles as [[Word Records]] attempted to wrest control of Squint from Taylor.<ref name="crossrhythms"/> This caused uncertainty with the band's future.<ref name="crossrhythms"/> Discussing the legal battle, bassist Joe Loeffler stated "we weren't sure if anything was going to happen after that, it was pretty crazy."<ref name="crossrhythms"/>

Chevelle toured as support to bands such as [[Sevendust]], [[Machine Head (band)|Machine Head]], [[Filter (band)|Filter]], and [[Powerman 5000]] in this period.<ref name="AMG" /><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik" /> Squint Entertainment closed down in 2001, and the band signed with [[Epic Records]] in 2002.<ref name="AMG"/> In 2002, Chevelle released its second studio album, ''[[Wonder What's Next]],'' on Epic Records.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref name="Wonder What's Next AllMusic">{{Cite web|first=Brian|last=O'Neill|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/wonder-whats-next-mw0000224363|title=Wonder What's Next Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013148/https://www.allmusic.com/album/wonder-whats-next-mw0000224363|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The band released the single "[[The Red (song)|The Red]]", which reached No.&nbsp;3 on the [[Hot Mainstream Rock Tracks|Mainstream rock charts]], and the video was played in regular rotation on [[MTV]].<ref name="Singles">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/rtt/|title=Chevelle Chart History – Singles|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013150/https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/rtt/|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Wonder What's Next'' peaked at No.&nbsp;14 on the United States [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] album chart.<ref name="Artist Chart History">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/tlp/|title=Chevelle Chart History: Billboard 200|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013148/https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/tlp/|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> Brian O'Neil of [[AllMusic]] stated the album "offers uniqueness not often heard in more commercial fare, no mean feat."<ref name="Wonder What's Next AllMusic"/> Chevelle released two more singles from the album, "[[Closure (Chevelle song)|Closure]]",<ref name="MTV Closure">{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Wiederhorn|url=https://www.mtv.com/news/1479210/chevelle-plan-headlining-tour-are-happy-to-offer-fans-closure/|title=Chevelle Plan Headlining Tour, Are Happy To Offer Fans 'Closure'|work=[[MTV]]|date=September 23, 2003|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927174656/https://www.mtv.com/news/1479210/chevelle-plan-headlining-tour-are-happy-to-offer-fans-closure/|archive-date=September 27, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> and "[[Send the Pain Below]]",<ref name="MTV Closure"/><ref name="Ozzfest">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-rumored-for-ozzfest-2003-main-stage|title=Chevelle Rumored For Ozzfest 2003 Main Stage|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 3, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024160819/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-rumored-for-ozzfest-2003-main-stage/|archive-date=October 24, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> the latter of which reached the No.&nbsp;1 position on both of the [[Mainstream Rock Chart|mainstream rock]] and [[Modern Rock Tracks chart|modern rock]] charts.<ref name="Singles"/> ''Wonder What's Next'' was certified 2× platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]] with excess sales of one million copies sold in the United States alone in 2003.<ref name="MusicomhreviewWWN">{{cite magazine|first=Tom|last=Day|url=http://www.musicomh.com/albums/chevelle.htm|title=Chevelle – Wonder What's Next (Epic)|magazine=[[MusicOMH]]|date=August 11, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071107073159/http://www.musicomh.com/albums/chevelle.htm|archive-date=November 7, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=Chevelle&ti=WONDER+WHAT%27S+NEXT#search_section|title=Chevelle – Wonder What's Next (Epic)|work=[[Recording Industry Association of America]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220515080729/https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=Chevelle&ti=WONDER+WHAT%27S+NEXT#search_section|archive-date=May 15, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Chevelle was nominated for three awards at the [[2003 Billboard Music Awards]].<ref name="Billboard Music Awards">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/67967/2003-billboard-music-awards-finalists|title=2003 Billboard Music Awards Finalists|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=December 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> One as a band and two for their song "Send the Pain Below".<ref name="Billboard Music Awards"/> The categories they were nominated for were Modern Rock Artist, Modern Rock Track, and [[Billboard Music Award for Top Rock Song|Top Rock Song]].<ref name="Billboard Music Awards"/>

In 2003, Chevelle performed at [[Ozzfest]],<ref name="Ozzfest"/> where the band recorded and later released its first [[live album]], ''[[Live from the Road]]'',<ref name="Live from the Road">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/68469/chevelle-polishes-live-from-the-road|title=Chevelle Polishes 'Live From The Road'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=October 24, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202100917/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/68469/chevelle-polishes-live-from-the-road|archive-date=December 2, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> and a live [[DVD]], ''Live from the Norva'' on October 14, 2003.<ref name="MTV Closure"/> In 2003, the band was featured on the [[Music as a Weapon Tour|Music as a Weapon II tour]] with [[Disturbed (band)|Disturbed]].<ref name="Live from the Road"/><ref name="Music as a Weapon II AM">{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Loftus|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/music-as-a-weapon-ii-mw0000322147|title=Music as a Weapon II - Disturbed|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013148/https://www.allmusic.com/album/music-as-a-weapon-ii-mw0000322147|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On the tour with Disturbed, Chevelle appeared on the tour compilation album, titled ''[[Music as a Weapon Tour#Music as a Weapon II|Music as a Weapon II]]'', featuring the songs "The Red" and "Forfeit".<ref name="Music as a Weapon II AM"/>  Keith Miller of EvangelSociety.org was critical of Chevelle for touring with Ozzfest with bands such as [[Cradle of Filth]], who he claimed incorporated strong Satanic and anti-Christian themes into their lyrics.<ref name="Over-reacter">{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Miller|url=http://www.evangelsociety.org/miller/chevelle2.html|title=Chevelle's Uncertain Witness|work=Evangel Society|date=February 9, 2004|access-date=December 25, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040504092216/http://www.evangelsociety.org/miller/chevelle2.html|archive-date=May 4, 2004|url-status=dead}}</ref> Chevelle held their first major headlining tour, from November 1 to December 17, 2003.<ref name="MTV Closure"/> The tour started in Cleveland and ended in Chicago.<ref name="MTV Closure"/> 

In 2004, Sam Loeffler said, "It's something that's probably going to follow us around forever and that's fine. It's pretty simple. We originally signed with a record company that was backed by [[Word Records|Word]] (a Christian label housing [[John Tesh]] and [[Amy Grant]]), so [''Point #1''] was in Christian bookstores. It was really an accidental thing".<ref name="Over-reacter" /><ref name="Christianity today">{{cite web|first=Andree|last=Farias|url=http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/glimpses/2004/thistypeofthinking.html|title=Chevelle This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In) (Epic)|work=Christianity Today|access-date=December 25, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071218201636/http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/glimpses/2004/thistypeofthinking.html|archive-date=December 18, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> Sam also told the ''Chicago Tribune'', "Our faith is still extremely important to us, but it's also very personal. None of us feels being a rock band on stage should be a pedestal for preaching".<ref name="Live From the Road review">{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Argyrakis|url=http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/reviews/2004/livefromtheroad.html|title=Chevelle Live From the Road (Epic)|work=Christianity Today|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071212062119/http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/reviews/2004/livefromtheroad.html|archive-date=December 12, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Line-up changes, ''This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)'', and ''Vena Sera'' (2004–2008) ===
{{Main|This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)|Vena Sera}}

''[[This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)]]'' was recorded in early 2004, and released on September 21, 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-set-release-date-for-new-album|title=Chevelle Set Release Date For New Album|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=July 13, 2004|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013152/https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-set-release-date-for-new-album|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=Melodic>{{cite web|url=http://melodic.net/?page=review&id=2915|title=Melodic Net - Chevelle - This Type of Thinking Could Do Us In|work=[[Melodic (magazine)|Melodic]]|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906090344/http://melodic.net/?page=review&id=2915|archive-date=September 6, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="This Type AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Loftus|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/this-type-of-thinking-could-do-us-in-mw0000152819|title=This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In) - Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013150/https://www.allmusic.com/album/this-type-of-thinking-could-do-us-in-mw0000152819|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The album debuted at No. 8 on the ''Billboard'' 200, and was certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] by the RIAA six weeks later.<ref name="Artist Chart History"/> Johnny Loftus of AllMusic described the songs on the album as "strong dynamically, but sound predetermined — they don't separate from the general loud rock malaise."<ref name="This Type AllMusic"/> The song "[[Vitamin R (Leading Us Along)]]" was released as the first single from the album and reached the No.&nbsp;1 position on the Mainstream Rock chart.<ref name="Singles"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.antimusic.com/news/04/dec/item16.shtml|title=Chevelle, Helmet Head SnoCore Tour|work=antiMusic|date=December 23, 2004|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050105095618/http://www.antimusic.com/news/04/dec/item16.shtml|archive-date=January 5, 2005|url-status=live}}</ref> Two other singles were released from the album, the titles of which are "[[The Clincher]]" peaking at No. 3 on the Mainstream rock chart, and "[[Panic Prone]]" which peaked at No. 26 on the same chart.<ref name="Singles"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/> The band's song "The Clincher" was featured in the video game ''[[Madden NFL 2005]]''.<ref name="The Clincher soundtrack">{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Cook|url=http://www.gameinformer.com/News/Story/200407/N04.0701.1627.08627.htm|title=EA Announces Madden NFL 2005 Soundtrack|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=July 1, 2004|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080122170824/http://www.gameinformer.com/News/Story/200407/N04.0701.1627.08627.htm|archive-date=January 22, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/07/01/madden-nfl-2005-busts-out-all-star-musical-line-up|title=Madden NFL 2005 Busts Out All-Star Musical Line-Up|work=[[IGN]]|date=June 17, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717002309/https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/07/01/madden-nfl-2005-busts-out-all-star-musical-line-up|archive-date=July 17, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

After the release of the album, Joe Loeffler was dismissed from Chevelle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/ex-chevelle-bassist-slams-former-bandmates-i-was-fired-plain-and-simple|title=Ex-Chevelle Bassist Slams Former Bandmates: 'I Was Fired, Plain And Simple'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=July 7, 2005|access-date=June 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213005327/https://blabbermouth.net/news/ex-chevelle-bassist-slams-former-bandmates-i-was-fired-plain-and-simple|archive-date=December 13, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Did Joe get fired">{{cite web|url=http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/chevelle_bassist_fired.html|title=Chevelle Bassist Fired?|work=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|date=July 4, 2005|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070503232838/https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/chevelle_bassist_fired.html|archive-date=May 3, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to different stories from the band members, it is unclear whether he was fired or left the band of his own accord.<ref name="Did Joe get fired"/> Pete and Sam stated the following on the band's official website: "After three years of non-stop touring and recording, Joe is taking a break to be home with family. We'll miss having him on the road with us, but as his brothers and bandmates we respect his decision and are looking forward to getting out there and playing for the fans. See you on tour." However, according to [[Ultimate Guitar Archive]], Joe said he was fired.<ref name="Did Joe get fired"/>

The band supported ''This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)'' with a headlining tour that included opening acts such as [[Taproot (band)|Taproot]] and [[Thirty Seconds to Mars]],<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/chevelle-taproot-team-for-summer-tour-62604/|title=Chevelle, Taproot Team For Summer Tour|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=June 13, 2005|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122161152/https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/chevelle-taproot-team-for-summer-tour-62604/|archive-date=November 22, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Harris|url=https://www.mtv.com/news/1503823/chevelle-taproot-30-seconds-to-mars-map-out-summer-tour/|title=Chevelle, Taproot, 30 Seconds To Mars Map Out Summer Tour|work=[[MTV]]|date=June 9, 2005|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412142151/https://www.mtv.com/news/1503823/chevelle-taproot-30-seconds-to-mars-map-out-summer-tour/|archive-date=April 12, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and continued playing small tours in 2005 with [[Geno Lenardo]] from the band [[Filter (band)|Filter]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-lineup-change-for-upcoming-tour|title=Chevelle: Lineup Change For Upcoming Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=June 30, 2005|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220613045029/https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-lineup-change-for-upcoming-tour|archive-date=June 13, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> In August 2005, the Loeffler brothers' brother-in-law, Dean Bernardini, joined the band as their bassist.<ref name="AMG" /><ref name="Did Joe get fired" /> In 2006, Chevelle supported [[Nickelback]] for an arena tour across the United States.<ref name="Did Joe get fired"/>

[[File:Pete Loeffler at 2007 MyCokeFest in Atlanta.JPG|thumb|Vocalist and guitarist Pete Loeffler performing in 2007 at MyCokeFest in Atlanta]]

In 2006, the band recorded their fourth studio album, ''[[Vena Sera]]''. The album was the first Chevelle recorded with Bernardini.<ref name="Vena Sera AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Apar|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/vena-sera-mw0000746725|title=Vena Sera Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013147/https://www.allmusic.com/album/vena-sera-mw0000746725|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Vena Sera'' was released on April 3, 2007,<ref name="Vena Sera AllMusic"/><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Michael|last=Endelman|url=https://ew.com/article/2007/03/30/vena-sera/|title=Vena Sera Review|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=April 6, 2007|access-date=June 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070421010156/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20016445,00.html|archive-date=April 21, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> debuting at No.&nbsp;12 on the ''Billboard'' 200, and sold 62,000 copies during its first week of release.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik" /><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Katie|last=Hasty|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1052919/now-24-trumps-duff-mcbride-timbaland-at-no-1|title=Now 24 Trumps Duff, McBride, Timbaland at No. 1|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=April 11, 2007|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130414015239/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1052919/now-24-trumps-duff-mcbride-timbaland-at-no-1|archive-date=April 14, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> The title of the album translates to "vein liquid" in Latin, representing the blood Chevelle put into making the album, according to Pete.<ref name="Journal">{{Cite web|first=Sam|last=Loeffler|url=http://www.chevelleinc.com/bandnotes_content.html|title=Band notes|publisher=Chevelle|access-date=December 25, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071208100937/http://www.chevelleinc.com/bandnotes_content.html|archive-date=December 8, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Corey Apar of AllMusic states that "''Vena Sera'' probably won't disappoint fans, and it didn't, if for the sole fact that it basically sounds just like Chevelle's other albums". He noted that the song "I Get It" "has a relatively lighter underbelly than the rest, which is a nice change of pace, but it's ultimately too little, too late".<ref name="Vena Sera AllMusic"/> "[[Well Enough Alone]]", the first single from the album, was written about the departure of Joe Loeffler, and reached No.&nbsp;4 on the Mainstream rock charts.<ref name="Singles"/> Chevelle toured with [[Evanescence]] and [[Finger Eleven]] during March and April 2007,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/evanescence-chevelle-finger-eleven-tour-dates-announced|title=Evanescence, Chevelle, Finger Eleven: Tour Dates Announced|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=January 19, 2007|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220613043755/https://blabbermouth.net/news/evanescence-chevelle-finger-eleven-tour-dates-announced|archive-date=June 13, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> followed by a headlining tour with Finger Eleven and [[Strata (band)|Strata]] in May and June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-extends-tour-into-june|title=Chevelle Extends Tour Into June|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=April 30, 2007|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126101953/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-extends-tour-into-june/|archive-date=November 26, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The second single from the album, "[[I Get It]]", was released on June 12, 2007, and a video for the song debuted on MTV on November 27, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/videos/chevelle/192012/i-get-it.jhtml#artist=509055|title=Chevelle I Get It – Premiere videos|work=[[MTV]]|date=November 27, 2007|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090114214553/http://www.mtv.com/videos/chevelle/192012/i-get-it.jhtml|archive-date=January 14, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July of the same year, Chevelle toured Australia as a supporting act for the band [[The Butterfly Effect (band)|The Butterfly Effect]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/the-butterfly-effect-imago-to-receive-u-s-release|title=The Butterfly Effect: 'Imago' To Receive U.S. Release|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=October 9, 2007|access-date=June 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143417/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-butterfly-effect-imago-to-receive-u-s-release/|archive-date=June 12, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> On the tour in Australia, Chevelle's band manager Rose died of cancer, much to the distress of the band.<ref name="Journal"/>

On May 9, 2007, during a show in [[Fort Worth, Texas]] Chevelle's trailer containing all of the band's equipment was stolen from the hotel at which the members were staying.<ref name="Fort Worth">{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=74673|title=Chevelle slowly recovering stonlen gear|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=June 14, 2007|access-date=August 12, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514131213/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=74673|archive-date=May 14, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band posted a notice saying, "Most items are labeled 'Chevelle' and if you notice anything suspicious on [[eBay]] or other online resellers selling 'authentic' Chevelle items... guitar, basses, drums, amplifiers, risers, backdrops, tee shirts... please call the police..." A month later in an interview, Sam Loeffler stated, "Of the 14 guitars, we got two of 'em, and then we got some amplifiers back and our monitor system. So it's really, I mean it's cool because it's kind of like Christmas, only really weird. People have been calling us and saying, 'Hey, I bought this or that', and you know, we're just doing our best to buy it back from them. And certainly the issue is not a money issue, it's about having the pieces of gear that you did all your records with."<ref name="Fort Worth"/>

=== ''Sci-Fi Crimes'' and ''Hats Off to the Bull'' (2009–2012) ===
{{Main|Sci-Fi Crimes|Hats Off to the Bull}}

[[File:Pete of Chevelle Live at the Carnival of Madness 2012.JPG|thumb|upright|Pete Loeffler performing live at the Carnival of Madness tour in 2012 at the Laredo Energy Arena]]
In 2009, Chevelle entered a studio in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]], [[Tennessee]] with producer Brian Virtue. Sam Loeffler stated, "We have spent a lot of time making these songs something different from past records without losing the core of our passion. We are a hard rock, melodic band and it's still what drives us as musicians."<ref name="Fifthystuff">{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=114802|title=Chevelle: Video footage from the studio posted online|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 20, 2009|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090312122822/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=114802|archive-date=March 12, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> The new album, titled ''[[Sci-Fi Crimes]]'' was released on August 31, 2009,<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Coplan|url=https://consequence.net/2009/08/chevelle-new-touralbum-to-be-so-good-its-criminal/|title=Chevelle new tour/album to be so good it's criminal|work=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|date=August 23, 2009|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717002309/https://consequence.net/2009/08/chevelle-new-touralbum-to-be-so-good-its-criminal/|archive-date=July 17, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="HM Sci-Fi Crimes">{{cite magazine|first=Doug|last=Van Pelt|url=https://hmmagazine.com/chevelle-announce-sci-fi-crimes-tour/|title=Chevelle Announce Sci-Fi Crimes Tour|magazine=[[HM (magazine)|HM]]|date=August 20, 2009|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305075654/https://hmmagazine.com/chevelle-announce-sci-fi-crimes-tour/|archive-date=March 5, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> peaking at No.&nbsp;6 on the ''Billboard'' 200 album chart with sales of about 46,000, the highest entry onto the chart to date for the band.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=126673|title=Chevelle's 'Sci-Fi Crimes' Cracks U.S. Top 10|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=September 9, 2009|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224164300/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-s-sci-fi-crimes-cracks-u-s-top/|archive-date=December 24, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="anylastwords">{{Cite web|url=http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=148614|title=Chevelle to release Any Last Words? DVD|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=October 31, 2010|access-date=May 18, 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201201836/http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=148614|archive-date=February 1, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album was praised by Jared Johnson of AllMusic for taking a step in a new direction in regards to the lyrics.<ref name="Sci-fi Crimes AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Jared|last=Johnson|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/sci-fi-crimes-r1626372/review|title=Sci-fi Crimes|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205130331/http://www.allmusic.com/album/sci-fi-crimes-r1626372/review|archive-date=December 5, 2010|url-status=live}}</ref> Pete Loeffler normally wrote lyrics about personal subjects, however on ''Sci-Fi Crimes'', he wrote of stories including apparitions, conspiracy theories, and erratic sleeping conditions.<ref name="Sci-fi Crimes AllMusic"/> The tour following the release of ''Sci-Fi Crimes'' was in the late 2009.<ref name="HM Sci-Fi Crimes"/> [[Halestorm]] opened for Chevelle on this tour.<ref name="HM Sci-Fi Crimes"/> Chevelle also joined Halestorm, [[Staind]], and [[Shinedown]] on "Stimulate This!" tour starting in July 2009.<ref name="Halestorm opening for Chevelle">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/staind-shinedown-chevelle-halestorm-to-team-up-for-stimulate-this-tour|title=Staind, Shinedown, Chevelle, Halestorm To Team Up For 'Stimulate This!' Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=May 11, 2009|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920214447/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/staind-shinedown-chevelle-halestorm-to-team-up-for-stimulate-this-tour/|archive-date=September 20, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

In January 2011, Chevelle released a live CD/DVD combo, ''Any Last Words''.<ref name="anylastwords"/> The release was part of Chevelle's ten-year anniversary as a recording band. As a special offer for fans, part of the pre-order package included a T-shirt and the fans' name in the 'thank yous' part of the album booklet.<ref name="anylastwords"/>

On December 6, 2011, Chevelle released ''[[Hats Off to the Bull]]'', their sixth studio album.<ref name="Hats Off to the Bull AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/hats-off-to-the-bull-r2334528/review|title=Hats Off to the Bull Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521215057/https://www.allmusic.com/album/hats-off-to-the-bull-mw0002253896|archive-date=May 21, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Pete|last=Crigler|url=http://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/152484-chevelle-hats-off-to-the-bull/|title=Chevelle-Hats Off to the Bull|magazine=[[PopMatters]]|date=January 4, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109032353/http://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/152484-chevelle-hats-off-to-the-bull/|archive-date=January 9, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album's first single was titled "[[Face to the Floor]]",<ref name="hatsoffdebut">{{cite web|url=http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=167236|title=Chevelle's 'Hats Off to the Bull' crack U.S. Top 20|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 1, 2013|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201111054/http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=167236|archive-date=February 1, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Liz|last=Ramanand|url=https://loudwire.com/chevelle-face-to-the-floor-song-review/|title=Chevelle, ‘Face to the Floor’ – Song Review|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=September 29, 2011|access-date=August 15, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719154213/https://loudwire.com/chevelle-face-to-the-floor-song-review/|archive-date=July 19, 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref> which reached No. 3 on ''Billboard'''s Rock songs chart.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/|title=Chevelle Active Rock|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013153/https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The album debuted at No.&nbsp;20 on the ''Billboard'' charts and sold 43,000 copies in its first week of release.<ref name="hatsoffdebut"/> Joe Barresi, who produced ''Hats Off to the Bull'' said of the album, "Rather than simply subscribing to a tried-and-true formula, they made a conscious effort to incorporate new sounds and textures into their patented airtight anthems. As a result, ''Hats Off to the Bull'' is one of the group's most infectious and impressive offerings to date."<ref name="hatsoffdebut"/> AllMusic reviewer Gregory Heaney stated the album is "Heavy and dramatic, the album is packed full of tightly coiled, muscular riffs, giving the album a controlled feeling more like a slow burn than an explosive, cathartic release."<ref name="Hats Off to the Bull AllMusic"/>

Chevelle was nominated for Rock Band of the Year at the 2012 Loudwire Music Awards.<ref name="Loudwire Music Awards 2012">{{cite web|url=https://loudwire.com/rock-band-of-the-year-2012-loudwire-music-awards/|title=Rock Band of the Year – 2012|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=December 4, 2012|access-date=January 11, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201127094334/https://loudwire.com/rock-band-of-the-year-2012-loudwire-music-awards/|archive-date=November 27, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Also, a compilation album of band favorites called ''[[Stray Arrows: A Collection of Favorites]]'', was released to stores on December 4, 2012.<ref name="Stray Arrows">{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Colgan|url=https://metalinsider.net/new-music/new-noteworthy-december-4th-same-old-trip|title=New & Noteworthy December 4th: Same Old Trip|work=Metal Insider|date=December 4, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220716054730/https://metalinsider.net/new-music/new-noteworthy-december-4th-same-old-trip|archive-date=July 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stray Arrows Loudwire">{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Bowar|url=https://loudwire.com/chevelle-greatest-hits-compilation-album-stray-arrows-december/|title=Chevelle to Release Greatest Hits Compilation Album 'Stray Arrows' in December|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=November 6, 2012|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220612062944/https://loudwire.com/chevelle-greatest-hits-compilation-album-stray-arrows-december/|archive-date=June 12, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stray Arrows Allmusic">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/mw0002443034|title=Stray Arrows: A Collection of Favorites - Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531114529/https://www.allmusic.com/album/mw0002443034|archive-date=May 31, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The compilation includes 11 songs and a previously unreleased track titled "Fizgig".<ref name="Stray Arrows"/><ref name="Stray Arrows Loudwire"/><ref name="Stray Arrows Allmusic"/> The [[Best Buy]] version has 15 songs and the track "Fizgig".<ref name="Stray Arrows"/>

=== ''La Gárgola'', ''The North Corridor'' and departure of Dean Bernardini (2013–2019) ===
{{Main|La Gárgola|The North Corridor}}
After wrapping up touring in support of ''Hats off to the Bull'' in 2013, Chevelle entered the studio to record their seventh album, re-teaming with [[Joe Barresi]] to produce the album.<ref name="banana1015">{{cite web|first=Tree|last=Riddle|url=http://banana1015.com/chevelle-drop-new-single-listen-to-take-out-the-gunman-audio/|title=Chevelle Drop New Single, Listen to 'Take Out The Gunman' [Audio]|work=Banana 101.5|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114153516/http://banana1015.com/chevelle-drop-new-single-listen-to-take-out-the-gunman-audio/|archive-date=January 14, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Recording and production finished early in 2014, and the band announced on February 1 that the album, to be released April 1, 2014, would be titled ''[[La Gárgola]]'' (Spanish for "the gargoyle").<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.antimusic.com/news/14/February/05Chevelle_Reveal_First_Song_From_New_Album.shtml|title=Chevelle Reveal First Song From New Album|work=antiMusic|date=February 5, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2014}}</ref><ref name="blabbermouth123">{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-la-gargola-artwork-track-listing-revealed/|title=Chevelle: 'La === ''NIRATIAS'' and ''Bright as Blasphemy'' (2019–present) ===
{{Main|NIRATIAS|Bright as Blasphemy}}
In June 2019, the band announced that they entered the studio with long-time producer [[Joe Barresi]].<ref name="Loudwire acoustic">{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/chevelle-acoustic-version-endlessly/|title=Chevelle Return With Acoustic Version of New Song 'Endlessly'|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=November 8, 2020|access-date=January 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108124830/https://loudwire.com/chevelle-acoustic-version-endlessly/|archive-date=November 8, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Along with the announcement drummer Sam Loeffler said they have been writing material for a year-and-a-half, meaning the process of making this album has taken longer than usual.<ref name="Loudwire acoustic"/> In an interview with KCAL 96.7's RadioActive Mike Z. in September 2019, vocalist Pete Loeffler stated:

{{Quote|"We went really dark on the last two [albums], really heavy and more metal. That’s personally where I like to be and I want to live on stage, but this record [Barresi] was like, ‘Let’s try to do some melodic stuff,’ so I went down that road."<ref name="Loudwire acoustic"/>}}

In a March 17, 2021, interview with Loudwire, Pete Loeffler states that despite the band selling over six million albums, they haven't gotten any money out of it. The money all went back to Epic. He blames it on signing a bad contract early on in his career.<ref>{{cite *"[[indie rock]]"<ref name="AMG"/> 
}}}}<!--End note-->
The band's debut album ''Point #1'' has been described as indie rock.<ref>{{cite web|first=Heather|last=Phares|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/point-1-mw0000239327|title=Point #1 - Chevelle &#124; Songs, Reviews, Credits, Awards|work=[[AllMusic]]|date=May 4, 1999|access-date=January 4, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150222062348/http://www.allmusic.com/album/point-1-mw0000239327|archive-date=February 22, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> The band's most popular albums, ''Wonder What's Next'' and ''This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)'', are both described as nu metal.<ref>{{cite web|first=J.R.|last=Scott|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2002/12/09/reader-review-wonder-whats-next|title=Reader Review: Wonder What's Next|work=[[IGN]]|date=December 9, 2002|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129173738/https://www.ign.com/articles/2002/12/09/reader-review-wonder-whats-next|archive-date=January 29, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mike|last=Schiller|url=http://www.popmatters.com/review/chevelle-thistype/|title=Chevelle: This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)|magazine=[[PopMatters]]|date=December 6, 2004|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305071411/http://www.popmatters.com/review/chevelle-thistype/|archive-date=March 5, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Wonder What's Next'' had been described as having a radio-friendly sound.<ref name="Sputnik The North Corridor">{{cite web|first=Raul|last=Stanciu|url=https://www.sputnikmusic.com/review/71164/Chevelle-The-North-Corridor/|title=Chevelle The North Corridor|work=[[Sputnikmusic]]|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2022}}</ref> Albums such as ''La Gargola'' and ''The North Corridor'' feature a heavier, more riff-oriented sound with lyrical themes influenced by horror.<ref name="Sputnik The North Corridor"/> Their ninth studio album ''NIRATIAS'' incorporated elements of [[progressive rock]] and [[art rock]] along with a science-fiction theme.<ref name="Consequence genres">{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Hadusek|url=https://consequence.net/2021/07/chevelle-2021-us-tour/|title=Chevelle Announce 2021 US Tou|work=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|date=July 26, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726155211/https://consequence.net/2021/07/chevelle-2021-us-tour/|archive-date=July 26, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

Their primary musical influences as stated by the band members are [[Helmet (band)|Helmet]],<ref name="AMG"/><ref name="KNAC interview">{{cite web|first=Charlie|last=Steffens|url=http://www.knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=3530|title=Exclusive! Interview With Chevelle Drummer Sam Loeffler|work=Knac|date=February 21, 2005|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100205062751/http://www.knac.com/article.asp?ArticleID=3530|archive-date=February 5, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Ultimate Guitar HOTTB rev">{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/reviews/compact_discs/chevelle/hats_off_to_the_bull/7987/|title=Hats Off To The Bull review by Chevelle|work=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|date=December 6, 2011|access-date=July 18, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220718185842/https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/reviews/compact_discs/chevelle/hats_off_to_the_bull/7987/|archive-date=July 18, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Tool (band)|Tool]],<ref name="AMG"/><ref name="KNAC interview"/><ref name="Ultimate Guitar HOTTB rev"/> and [[The Cure]].<ref name="Ultimate Guitar HOTTB rev"/> Chevelle has frequently been compared to Tool throughout its career.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Harris|url=https://noisecreep.com/chevelle-know-they-sound-like-tool-slam-auto-tune-lovers-fall-o/|title=Chevelle Know They Sound like Tool, Slam Auto-Tune Lovers Fall Out Boy|work=[[Noisecreep]]|date=August 19, 2009|access-date=January 4, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220716044334/https://noisecreep.com/chevelle-know-they-sound-like-tool-slam-auto-tune-lovers-fall-o/|archive-date=July 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Pete Loeffler's singing voice was stated to sound similar to that of Tool's [[Maynard James Keenan]],<ref name="renownedforsound La Gárgola"/> and the band's music has been compared to Tool's "soft-loud vocal dynamics."<ref name="AMG"/> According to Lauren Wise of ''[[Phoenix New Times]]'', "[Chevelle have] never strayed far from their controlled chaos and somehow gentle rampage or their mix of dark magnetism and gothic pop (think early Tool meets The Cure if you haven't heard radio-dominating hits like "The Red")."<ref>{{cite web|first=Lauren|last=Wise|url=https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/music/chevelles-pete-loeffler-loves-the-80s-gun-wielding-fans-not-so-much-6597579|title=Chevelle's Pete Loeffler Loves the '80s; Gun-Wielding Fans? Not So Much|work=[[Phoenix New Times]]|date=April 26, 2012|access-date=January 4, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220716044334/https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/music/chevelles-pete-loeffler-loves-the-80s-gun-wielding-fans-not-so-much-6597579|archive-date=July 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

Despite comparisons to Tool, many critics such as Andree Farias and Andy Argyrakis of ''Christianity Today'' have stated Chevelle as having a unique sound to their music.<ref name="Christianity today"/><ref name="Live From the Road review"/> Andree Farias of ''Christianity Today'' has reviewed Chevelle's first three albums, praising them as "commanding vocals over jolting guitars and chest-thumping bass beats".<ref name="Christianity today" /> In discussing the band's sound throughout their career, Raul Stanciu of ''Sputnikmusic'' stated, "It amazes me how Chevelle manage to maintain such a consistent output...[they're] always tweaking the overall sound in small amounts, so that you’ll be constantly surprised."<ref name="Sputnik The North Corridor"/> Chevelle's music has also been described as "a kind of controlled chaos, a beautiful darkness, a gentle rampage of aural velocity."<ref name="lasvegasmagazine1"/>
